name: Filippo Arena
bornNote: BORN AND BAPTISED THE SAME DAY at Scilla -- «infantem HODIE NATUM» -- and given the name PHILIPPUS NUNTIATUS. The extract was copied from the parish book of baptisms on 26 May 1815 for his own marriage file. It replaces the «c. 1794» this archive carried from his statement at his son's birth registration in 1819, where he gave his age as twenty-five; he was twenty-six.
source: Scilla, Nati 1819 atto 186; Matrimoni 1851 atto 13; Nati 1861 atto 228; Scilla, Nati 1819 atto 186 read in the processetti of 1851
note: Named in FOUR independent acts. The sea trade runs Orazio -> Filippo -> Francesco Antonio -> Rocco, four generations of sailors, and he was a MARINARO himself at twenty-two. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. HE WAS ALSO, FOR FIVE DAYS, THE ARCHIVE'S PUBLISHED WALL -- «his marriage to Domenica Costa is pre-civil, the Arena line stops here» -- because this archive believed Scilla's registers began in 1816. THEY BEGIN IN 1809. He married Domenica Costa on 12 NOVEMBER 1815, Matrimoni atto 29, and the act names his parents ORAZIO ARENA and LITTERIA MORABITO, both alive and both standing beside him, because at twenty-two he was still a minor under the code. Every negative reported for 1816 to 1819 was correct; the conclusion drawn from them was not. AND HE COULD WRITE: he signed his own marriage act «Filippo Arena sposo», and signed his son's birth act in 1819, in registers where almost nobody signs.

name: Domenica Costa
bornNote: BORN AND BAPTISED THE SAME DAY at Scilla, by the archpriest Giuseppe Ingigneri himself, and given the name DOMINICA JOSEPHA. This settles a five-year disagreement in this archive's favour of neither guess: she was twenty-eight at her marriage in November 1815, which fits exactly, and THIRTY-TWO -- not twenty-seven -- when her son Francesco Antonio was born in November 1819. The age in that birth act is five years wrong.
source: Scilla, Nati 1819, atto 186; Scilla, Nati 1819 atto 186 read in the processetti of 1851
note: Filippo Arena's wife, and now one of the best-attested people in this archive: her baptism of 1787, her marriage of 1815, her son's birth in 1819. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. Her parents are GIOVANNI DE COSTA, dead at Scilla on 29 March 1790 when she was two, and MARTA ALFONZETTI, who was still alive to consent to the marriage twenty-five years later. NOTE THE SURNAME: Costa is also what her great-grandson Rocco married, in Generosa Costa, and a Lorenzo Costa was lodging with Rocco in New York in 1900. THIS ROW ONCE SAID «HER MARRIAGE IS OUT OF REACH». It was in a volume nobody had opened, four years before the window this archive had drawn for itself.

name: Francesco Antonio Arena
bornNote: Act 186 of 1819. Act 228 of 1861 makes him 42 on 23 December 1861 -- forty-two years and one month. The fit is exact.
source: Scilla, Nati 1819 atto 186; Nati 1860 atto 45; Nati 1861 atto 228
note: ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE, which puts Rocco Arena under Orazio Arena instead. He and Serafina Arlotta have a son Giuseppe on 5 March 1860 and a son Rocco on 20 December 1861 -- exactly the sibling pair the tree assigns to Orazio.

name: Serafina Arlotta
bornNote: Act 2 of 1830. Twenty at her marriage on 7 February 1851 -- exact. Act 228 of 1861 makes her 28, which is three years adrift; she was 31.
source: Scilla, Nati 1830 atto 2; Matrimoni 1851 atto 13; Nati 1861 atto 228
note: ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. Her parents are now confirmed twice over: Giovanni Arlotta, marinaro, and Maria Costa.

name: Filippo Arena (the younger)
bornNote: Act 48 of 1852.
source: Scilla, Nati 1852, atto 48
note: Rocco Arena's eldest brother, named for their grandfather Filippo. Not in the family tree.

name: Domenica Arena
bornNote: ACT 53 of 1853 -- not act 2, which is a Tavola row number. Born at twelve o'clock on 24 March 1853 in her parents' own house and declared the same afternoon by her father.
source: Scilla, Nati 1853 atto 53, read in the original
note: ROCCO ARENA'S SISTER, NOT HIS BROTHER -- and this archive carried her as a son for weeks. The act says «una FEMINA», then «di dare alla FANCIULLA il nome di DOMENICA», and the baptism column names DOMENICA ARENA. Three statements in one act, none ambiguous. Her father is written out in full as FRANCESCANTONIO ARENA, thirty-two, MARINARO -- exact for a birth on 25 November 1819 -- and her mother SERAFINA ARLOTTA, twenty-two, exact for 13 June 1830. Not in the family tree. IT ALSO REMOVES A MYSTERY: a daughter who married leaves the Arena surname, so «Domenico Arena disappears after 1853» was never a disappearance.

name: Teresa Arena
bornNote: Act 6 of 1853.
source: Scilla, Nati 1853, atto 6
note: Orazio Arena's earliest known child. Not in the family tree -- which gives Orazio only the two children who turn out to be Francesco Antonio's.

name: Giovanni Arena (b. 1854)
bornNote: Scilla, act 76 of 1854, at nine in the morning, in his parents' house. NOT 20 April, and not the son of a Rosa Arlotta -- the annual Tavola is wrong on both counts and the act is right.
source: Scilla, Nati 1854, atto 76
note: ROCCO ARENA'S ELDER BROTHER. His birth act names his father ANTONIO ARENA, thirty-four -- Francesco Antonio, born 25 November 1819, is exactly thirty-four in April 1854 -- and his mother SERAFINA ARLOTTA, and it was declared by his maternal grandfather GIOVANNI ARLOTTA, who gave the boy his own name. This is the Giovanni Arena who sails in 1899 to join 'brother Rocco' and enters six-year-old Anna as his NIECE. HE IS IN THE FAMILY TREE, and this archive said for a time that he was not: the tree's Giovanni Arena, husband of Concetta Russo, IS this man, dated 1870 there and born in fact on 30 April 1854. What the act adds is sixteen years and two parents, not a person.

name: Giovanni Arlotta
bornNote: TWENTY-EIGHT at his own marriage on 30 August 1828. His daughter's birth act of 1830 makes him forty and his grandson's of 1854 makes him seventy-five -- three of his own declarations, twenty-one years apart. The marriage act is preferred: it is the one where age carried legal weight and it names his parents. A FOURTH DECLARATION, from 24 Nov 2026: in his son Antonio's birth act of 3 October 1834 (Scilla Nati 1834 atto 163) he gives his age as forty-five, which would make him born about 1789 -- eleven years older than the marriage act's twenty-eight. The stated ages (28 in 1828, 40 in 1830, 45 in 1834, 75 in 1854) do not agree with each other; the marriage act is still preferred, and the spread is the point.
source: Scilla, Nati 1854 atto 76; Matrimoni 1851 atto 13; Nati 1830 atto 2; Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 28; Nati 1834 atto 163; Morti 1865 atto 136
note: Serafina Arlotta's father, so Rocco Arena's maternal grandfather. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. A sailor. NOW IN THREE ACTS AND DATED: the marriage act of 1851, his daughter's birth act of 1830, and the birth act of 1854 in which he appears IN PERSON, aged seventy-five, to declare his grandson -- and which names HIS OWN FATHER, Domenico. ALIVE ON 23 JULY 1865: the death act of his son Antonio Arlotta (Morti 1865 atto 136) names «Giovanni, marinaro, domiciliato in Scilla» and Maria Costa with no «fu», and the A section of the 1865 death Tavola has no Giovanni Arlotta, so his own death is after 1865 (the Italian-era Scilla deaths) -- or at Scilla after August 1865. Read 24 Nov 2026. A CANDIDATE DEATH, 25 Nov 2026 (NOT an identification): the alphabetical index of the Scilla Morti 1866 volume (an_ua16601177, image 52, A block) lists «Arlotta Giovanni», register number 12, which would be a death between 1 January and mid-April 1866, after the July 1865 sighting. The index gives no patronymic or age, and the act cannot be read: this volume's first act is number 49, dated 18 April 1866 (image 2), so acts 1 to 48 are not in it and have not been found on Antenati. The same index lists Arlotta Rocco (1 and 133), Teresa (143) and Antonio (186). Another man of the name could be meant.

name: Maria Costa
bornNote: TWENTY-SIX at her marriage on 30 August 1828, with both her parents standing beside her and giving formal consent. CORRECTED THE SAME DAY IT WAS FIRST WRITTEN: her daughter's birth act of 1830 makes her twenty-three, which this archive entered as «c. 1807» that morning. Her own marriage act outranks her husband's statement at a registration desk.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1851 atto 13; Nati 1830 atto 2; Scilla, Nati 1830 atto 89 read in the processetti of 1851; Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 28; Nati 1834 atto 163 (aged thirty there)
note: Giovanni Arlotta's wife. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. NOTE THE SURNAME: she is the SECOND Costa in this generation -- Filippo Arena's wife is Domenica Costa -- and their great-grandson Rocco married a THIRD, Generosa Costa. A Lorenzo Costa was also lodging with Rocco in New York in 1900. CONFIRMED TWICE, by the 1851 marriage act and the 1830 birth act.

name: Gaetano Bonanno
bornNote: AGED THIRTY-SIX at his daughter Leonarda's birth in November 1843, so born about 1807. Piedimonte Etneo.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1843 atto 101; Matrimoni 1871 atto 14; Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni allegati 1871, fascicolo 14 -- «CERTIFICATO di seguita pubblicazione di matrimonio senza opposizione», 16 April 1871
note: Leonarda Bonanno's father. The archive had only the bare first name 'Gaetano', from a marriage proclamation of 1910; he is now in two registers with his surname, his trade and his age. ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE FAMILY TREE. ALIVE ON 16 APRIL 1871: «figlia del VIVENTE GAETANO, professione bracciante, residente anche ivi», in his daughter Leonarda's publication certificate. Aged about sixty-four and still at Piedimonte.

name: Anna Cavallaro
bornNote: AGED THIRTY-EIGHT at Leonarda's birth in November 1843, so born about 1805.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1843 atto 101; Matrimoni 1871 atto 14; Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni allegati 1871, fascicolo 14 -- «CERTIFICATO di seguita pubblicazione di matrimonio senza opposizione», 16 April 1871
note: Gaetano Bonanno's wife, named in the register. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE -- and mind the namesake: the tree does hold an Anna Cavallaro, but she is the daughter of a Luciano Cavallaro BORN IN 1945 and has nothing to do with this woman, who was having children in the 1830s. Two different people, a century and a half apart. ALIVE ON 16 APRIL 1871: «e della VIVENTE ANNA CAVALLARO, professione industriosa, residente anche ivi». First record of her trade, and a proof of life twenty-eight years after Leonarda's birth.

name: Domenico Arlotta
bornNote: NINETY-FIVE at his death on 17 March 1823 («di anni novantacinque», Scilla Morti 1823 atto 27, read at the image), so born about 1727-28; a stated age, so only about. Pre-civil: his baptism would be a parish record.
father: Arlotta, Antonio (father of Domenico Arlotta, d. before 1823)
mother: Domenica Cosentino (mother of Domenico Arlotta, d. before 1823)
source: Scilla, Morti 1823 atto 27 (an_ua2002677, image 15, right page; Tavola 1823 entry 2 on image 68); Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 28; Nati 1854 atto 76
note: FOUND: DOMENICO ARLOTTA DIED AT SCILLA ON 17 MARCH 1823, in his own house at ten in the morning, a marinaro born at Scilla, «vedovo di Francesca Paladino» and husband of Anna Barbaro (Morti 1823 atto 27, declared at two in the afternoon of the same day by Francesco Messina (about forty, marinaro) and Pietro Bova (about thirty-three, industriante), both of Scilla), son of the late Antonio Arlotta and the late Domenica Cosentino. The identification with Giovanni Arlotta's father rests on the name, the trade, the date (dead before 30 August 1828) and above all his wife Anna Barbaro, who is the mother named in Giovanni's marriage act; he is the only Arlotta Domenico in the 1823 Tavola. His age (95) sits awkwardly beside a son born about 1779 (75 in 1854) or about 1800 (28 in 1828) -- 51 or 72 at the birth -- and a first wife Francesca Paladino, so Anna Barbaro was probably a second wife; the age is the clerk's and is not settled. EARLIER NOTE KEPT: he is «fu Domenico Arlotta» in his son's marriage act of 30 August 1828 and was named in his grandson's birth act of 30 April 1854. Read 24 Nov 2026; the Tavolas of 1819, 1822, 1824, 1826, 1827 and 1828 hold no Domenico Arlotta.

name: Concetta Russo
bornNote: Aged TWENTY-SIX at her marriage in October 1885, so born about 1859. Scilla.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1885, atto 86
note: GIOVANNI ARENA'S WIFE. IN THE FAMILY TREE, which gives her no dates and no parents; the register gives both. Her age of thirty-three in her son Giuseppe's birth act of October 1892 puts her birth about 1859, and the same act names her parents LEONARDO RUSSO and ANGELA BAGNATO -- and those two are genuinely absent from the tree.

name: Leonardo Russo
bornNote: Not sought.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1885, atto 86
note: Concetta Russo's father, living at Scilla in 1885. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE.

name: Angela Bagnato
bornNote: Not sought.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1885, atto 86
note: Concetta Russo's mother, living at Scilla in 1885. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE.

name: Maria Martello
bornNote: Aged TWENTY-FOUR at her marriage in September 1885.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1885, atto 73
note: Giuseppe Arena's wife -- Giuseppe being Rocco Arena's brother, born 5 March 1860. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. Her father PAOLO MARTELLO was already RESIDENT IN AMERICA in 1885.

name: Anna Arlotta
bornNote: Not yet sought.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1888, atto 63
note: Generosa Costa's mother, named for the first time. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. AND NOTE THE SURNAME: Rocco Arena's mother is Serafina ARLOTTA and his wife's mother is Anna ARLOTTA. Whether they were sisters has not been tested, but if they were, Rocco and Generosa were first cousins.

name: Fortunato Arena
bornNote: Ten days old when he died on 1 October 1891, so born about the 21st of September. Via Grotte 70, Scilla.
source: Scilla, Morti 1891, atto 134
note: A son of ROCCO ARENA'S BROTHER Giovanni, dead at ten days. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. His death act fixes the household at VIA GROTTE -- the same street where his brother Giuseppe would be born thirteen months later, at number 75 -- and calls his father a PESCATORE, as Giuseppe's birth act does.

name: Antonio Costa
bornNote: AGED FORTY-EIGHT at his daughter Generosa's banns in November 1888, so born about 1840.
source: Scilla, Pubblicazioni 1888 no. 63; Matrimoni 1888 atto 63
note: Generosa Costa's father, now dated and with a trade. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE.

name: Maria Donato
bornNote: Twenty-eight months old when she died on 16 February 1891, so born about October 1888. Via Grotte 21, Scilla.
source: Scilla, Morti 1891, atto 22
note: A daughter of MICHELE DONATO and MARIA SOFI, and a sister of Nunziata Donato, dead at two years and four months. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. Her death act gives her father's trade -- PESCATORE -- and the family's address. UPDATE 18 NOVEMBER 2026: HER BIRTH ACT, Scilla Nati 1888 atto 229 (an_ua16601253, image 103): made on the 21st (read with a query) of October 1888 at 10.17 in the morning before the assessore delegato Luigi Minasi; born the same day at about 8.50 in the morning (day and hour doubtful), to Michele Donato, 33, marinaro, who declared her and signed, and Maria Sofi, his wife, a spinner living with him; the witnesses Giuseppe Arlotta? or Bellotta? and Guglielmo Nicola? (surnames and ages doubtful), who could not sign. This dates her birth to October 1888 and agrees with the 28 months of her death act.

name: Annunziata Donato (b. 1892, of Michele Donato and Maria Sofi)
bornNote: Born at half past four in the afternoon on 6 July 1892 at via Grotte no. 31 (Scilla, Nati 1892 atto 162, an_ua16601257, image 56); the act was made on 7 July at 9.15 before the assessore Gaetano D'Amico.
source: Scilla, Nati 1892 atto 162 (an_ua16601257, image 56, right page, lower act)
note: THE TREE'S NUNNZIATA DONATO, read at the image: the act names her Annunziata, and the parents are Michele Donato, 36, pescatore (who declared her) and Maria Sofi, his wife, a spinner living with him. The witnesses were Giuseppe Arlotta (56) and Antonio Ponte? (38), both pescatori and unable to sign. A margin note appears to read that she died at Scilla on 26 August 1975 (death act of Scilla 1975, no. 30), but the 9 of the year is faint and the note is not checked against the death act, so no death is recorded here.

name: Santa Donato (b. 1900, of Michele Donato and Maria Sofi)
bornNote: Born at half past eight in the morning on 13 March 1900 at via Grotte no. 30 (Scilla, Nati 1900 atto 65, an_ua16601265, image 24); the act was made on 16 March before the sindaco Rocco Minasi.
died: 21 September 1953, at Villa San Giovanni (a margin note on the birth act, registered 6 April 1954)
source: Scilla, Nati 1900 atto 65 (an_ua16601265, image 24)
note: THE SECOND SANTA, and the tree's Santa Donato (wife of a Salvatore, with a son Peppe, no dates) is taken to be her because the first Santa is not known to have lived past infancy; that is an inference and not a record. Michele, 44, pescatore, declared her; the witnesses Antonino Borni? (73) and Antonio Alfonsetti? (36), both pescatori and unable to sign. The margin note says she died at Villa San Giovanni on 21 September 1953, the entry stamped on 6 April 1954.

name: Domenico Donato (b. 1896, of Michele Donato and Maria Sofi)
bornNote: Born on 22 October 1896 (the day is written ventidue, the same as the act's date; read twice); the act, Scilla Nati 1896 atto 225 (an_ua16601261, image 76), was made on 22 October before the sindaco Raffaele Minasi.
source: Scilla, Nati 1896 atto 225 (an_ua16601261, image 76)
note: A SON OF MICHELE DONATO AND MARIA SOFI, and the tree's Domenico Donato (who has no dates and a wife named Rosina) is taken to be him on his name and parents alone: a Domenico born after 1900, when the registers online end, would be another man, so the join is the tree's own and not a second proof. Michele, 41, pescatore, declared the birth; the witnesses Santo Pesina? (36, pescatore) and Antonio Bosini or Rosmi? (about 60, pescatore), neither able to sign; the hour is doubtful.

name: Santa Donato (b. 1895, of Michele Donato and Maria Sofi)
bornNote: Born at a quarter past four in the afternoon on 16 March 1895 at via Grotte no. 25 (Scilla, Nati 1895 atto 70, an_ua16601260, image 25); the act was made on 17 March at 8.40 before the assessore Gaetano D'Amico. The act gives Michele's age as 38 (he was 39).
source: Scilla, Nati 1895 atto 70 (an_ua16601260, image 25); the year has no annual index and the act was found by reading the act headings of acts 1 to 84
note: A DAUGHTER OF MICHELE DONATO AND MARIA SOFI, THE FIRST SANTA, AND TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE with her sister of 1900 who has the same name: the name was given again in March 1900, which is the usual sign that this child had died, and she must have died before then (her death is not in the registers read, and nobody has looked for it). Michele declared her, a pescatore; the witnesses were Raffaele Perina? (65, pescatore) and a man written Sofi Nunzio or Remigio (50, pescatore), who bears the mother's surname and may be a relative. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE.

name: Francesco Giovanni Rocco Arena
bornNote: Ten months old when he died on 30 June 1898, so born about August 1897. Via Acquagrande 30, Scilla.
source: Scilla, Morti 1898, atto 91
note: A NEPHEW OF ROCCO ARENA -- son of his brother Giuseppe and Maria Martello -- dead at ten months. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. His three given names are his paternal grandfather and both his uncles: FRANCESCO for Francesco Antonio Arena, GIOVANNI and ROCCO for his father's brothers.

name: Domenico Donato
bornNote: EXACT, from his own birth act copied into his marriage bundle — Scilla, Nati 1816, atto 207, declared by his father the day he was born. It agrees to the day with the thirty-eight he is given at his son Michele's birth on 3 October 1855.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845, fascicolo 20 (Nati 1816 atto 207; Nati 1818 atto 129); Matrimoni 1844 atto 20; Nati 1855 atto 163
note: MICHELE DONATO'S FATHER, and a great-great-grandfather of the two children. A sailor, like the Arena men. HE IS IN THE FAMILY TREE as Michele's father and nothing more -- no dates, no trade, no parents. This archive claimed for a time that he was absent; that was wrong. What is new is everything else about him: born about 1817, MARINARO, and son of CANDELORO DONATO and MARIA PALADINO, who are absent. UPDATE 18 NOVEMBER 2026, A CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO COPIES OF ONE ACT: the register itself (Scilla Nati 1816 atto 207, an_ua2002801, image 108, right page, re-zoomed by the session) reads «è comparso DOMENICO Donato d'anni trentatre, Marinaro» as the declarant, the child a boy born at eleven o'clock the same day and named Domenico, and the mother SANTA Paladino, thirty, his lawful wife; the date word is Diciassette or Diciotto, not settled at the heading. The copy in the 1844 marriage bundle, as this row was first written, gave the father as CANDELORO. The act is a faded, ink-blotted page and the declarant's name may be the clerk's slip for the child's own name; Candeloro is the father in the acts of 1818 and 1823 and in the 1844 papers, so the line to Candeloro is KEPT, but the 1816 act alone does not support it and must not be quoted as naming him.

name: Nunziata Sofi
bornNote: From her own birth act copied into her marriage bundle — Scilla, Nati 1818, atto 129. Agrees with the thirty-seven she is given at her son's birth in October 1855.
died: 8 June 1901, at via Grotte, Scilla (Morti 1901 atto 74)
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845, fascicolo 20 (Nati 1816 atto 207; Nati 1818 atto 129)
note: MICHELE DONATO'S MOTHER. IN THE FAMILY TREE, under the fuller form ANNUNZIATA SOFI, with no dates and no parents. Her son married a SOFI in his turn -- Maria Sofi -- and named his daughter NUNZIATA for her. What the 1844 Tavola adds is her parents, PASQUALE SOFI and MARIA DE AMICO, who are absent. UPDATE 18 NOVEMBER 2026, HER DEATH: Scilla Morti 1901 atto 74 (an_ua16601213, image 38, re-zoomed by the session): «SOFI ANNUNZIATA, di anni ottantaquattro circa» (she was 82: the age is the act's and not relied on), died at 2.25 in the afternoon of 8 June 1901 in via Grotte, born at Scilla, DAUGHTER OF THE LATE PASQUALE, pescatore, AND THE LATE MARIA D'AMICO, casalinga, and WIDOW OF DONATO DOMENICO; declared by the gravediggers Filippo Arena and Domenico Tescoriere?, the witnesses Pasquale Defrancesco (48, terrazziere) and Angelo Labate? (43, panettiere), before the assessore Gaetano D'Amico. Her parents are the same pair as Domenico Sofi's, so they were brother and sister, and the widow of Domenico Donato is Michele Donato's mother, who lived to see his children born.

name: Candeloro Donato
bornNote: THIRTY-THREE when he declared his son Domenico's birth on 18 December 1816, so born about 1783. The first age this archive has ever had for him. (18 November 2026: the register's own act 207 names the declarant Domenico Donato, not Candeloro; see Domenico Donato b. 1816. The age 33 is the age that act gives its declarant, so the date c. 1783 is only as good as the identification, and is supported otherwise by the age 38 in 1823.)
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845, fascicolo 20 (Nati 1816 atto 207; Nati 1818 atto 129); Matrimoni 1845, atto 31
note: THE OLDEST DONATO, and now dated. A sailor, like his son and his grandson. He was alive when his son Michele married in August 1845 -- «FIGLIO DI Candeloro Donato», not «del fu» -- and alive the year before too: his son Domenico's marriage bundle of July 1844 runs to FIVE FOGLI and contains no death certificate for either father, which this series required when a parent had died. HE IS WHERE THE SCILLA LINE STOPS. His own marriage, and any birth of his own, fall before 1816 when Scilla's civil registration begins, and his son Michele was born at MESSINA about 1814 where registration does not begin until 1820. Everything earlier is a parish record.

name: Rocco Arlotta
bornNote: Aged twenty-two at his marriage in June 1900.
source: FindMyPast, United States Marriages; US census 1900
note: THE ARLOTTA IN ROCCO ARENA'S HOUSEHOLD in the Manhattan census of June 1900, now identified: he married ANTONIETTA TAVANI in Manhattan on 4 June that same month. His father was ANTONIO Arlotta -- NOT the Giovanni Arlotta who was Serafina's father -- so he is not her nephew; a cousin is likelier and is untested. He stayed in New York: a Rocco Arlotta baptises children at Our Lady of Loretto, the Arena's own parish, in 1905 and 1908. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE.

name: Antonino Prostamo
died: 31 December 1837, at Pizzo, in the cholera
source: Briatico, Matrimoni 1849, atto 1 — Antenati an_ua87663
note: The fourth generation, carried as UNTESTED until 14 September 2026 and now documented four times over. A MARINARO like his father and his son. He died at two in the morning on the last night of 1837 and his death is entered in Pizzo's SEPARATE REGISTER OF CHOLERA DEATHS, atto 327 — which is why the ordinary Morti volumes do not hold him. IN THE FAMILY TREE as antonino-prostamo-1785, where he is dated 1785 and given Pasquale Prostamo and a «Caterina Di Meio» as parents; the Pizzo register calls that same wife CATERINA MAJO.

name: Caterina Cichello
bornNote: TWENTY-SIX at her marriage on 2 March 1824, and BORN AT ZAMBRONE — so born about 1798, which agrees with the about-1799 this archive already had from her daughter's marriage bundle.
source: Zambrone, Matrimoni 1824, atto 2; Briatico, Matrimoni 1849, atto 1; Briatico, Matrimoni 1838, atto 2 (an_ua87652, image 3, read at the image by the session); Briatico, Morti 1849, atto 21 (an_ua87707, image 12, read at the image by the session)
note: GIOVANNA VENTRICE'S MOTHER, and now with parents. She married GIUSEPPE VENTRICE at ZAMBRONE on 2 MARCH 1824, and the act names her «figlia DEL FU FRANCESCO e DELLA FU VITTORIA MOLLO» -- both already dead when she married at twenty-six. She was widowed in June 1831, eighteen years before she appears alive at Briatico in her daughter's marriage papers of 1849. SHE MARRIED AGAIN, at Briatico on 1 OCTOBER 1838 (promise act no. 2, the notice posted Sunday 2 September 1838): GIACOMO COMERCI, 53, a miller (magnaio), born Briatico. The act names her «Caterina Cichello», aged «quaran[ta]…» (the number is not completed), «nata in Zambrone», domiciled at Briatico, «figlia di Francesco Cichello, bracciale, defunto, e di Vittoria Mollo (written Mollo/Molto), defunta», so the same two parents as in 1824, and no other Caterina Cichello fits them. The act does not say «vedova»; she was Giuseppe Ventrice's widow by the death act of June 1831. Giacomo Comerci is the miller who DECLARED Giuseppe Ventrice's death in 1831. Witnesses Giuseppe Lia and Antonio Orlando. Nothing is known of whether she had further children. ALIVE ON 10 NOVEMBER 1849, five months after that marriage: her son Giovanni's death act names her, with no «fu», as «domiciliata in Briatico» (Morti 1849, atto 21), and her second husband Giacomo Comerci had died on 24 May 1848 (Morti 1848, atto 6), so she is a widow twice over by then. Her own death is not in the Briatico death books of 1840-58 (1849 and 1850-58 read, three of them thin); it falls after November 1849, and after 1858 nothing is on Antenati for Briatico.

name: Caterina Majo
source: Pizzo, Morti 1829, atto 7 — Antenati an_ua37926878
note: Pasquale Prostamo's wife, named because he is recorded as her WIDOWER; dead by January 1829. The family tree has no wife for the third generation. THIS ARCHIVE FIRST PUBLISHED HER AS «CATERINA MUSO». That was a misreading: the surname is MAJO in the original register and in the chancery's own certified copy of 1849, compared side by side.

name: Maria Fragalà
source: Pizzo, Nati 1814, atto 285; Pizzo morti colerici 1837, atto 327; Briatico, Matrimoni 1849, atto 1
note: Twenty-seven when her son was born in April 1814, so born about 1787. WIDOWED BY THE CHOLERA on the last night of 1837 and still living at Pizzo in June 1849, when her son married eleven kilometres away at Briatico. SHE IS IN THE FAMILY TREE, dated 1789 and married to Antonino Prostamo; this archive said for a time that she was not in it at all, which was wrong and is corrected here. What the Briatico act of 1849 adds is her widowhood, her town and her age.

name: Domenico Ventrice
source: Zambrone, Morti 1815, atto 40 — certified extract in Briatico, Matrimoni processetti 1849-1854
note: Giovanna Ventrice's paternal grandfather, and the reason his certificate is in her marriage bundle: the act says she produced «la fede di morte del padre e dell'avo paterno», and the bundle holds exactly two Ventrice deaths. Died at Zambrone on 13 January 1815 at twenty-three o'clock, a BRACCIALE, husband of ANNA FAMA, and son of the late PAOLO VENTRICE and the late ANNA PAPPA. HIS AGE IS AMBIGUOUS IN THE ONLY SURVIVING TEXT: the copyist writes «sposo di Anna Fama di anni cinquanta ... di anni cinquantotto, di professione bracciale». The fifty-eight sits with his trade and is taken as his, so born about 1757; the fifty is taken as his wife's. This archive first published him as fifty.

name: Anna Fama
source: Zambrone, Morti 1815, atto 40; Briatico, Morti 1839, atto 12
note: Domenico Ventrice's wife and Giuseppe Ventrice's mother. Given as «di anni cinquanta» in her husband's death act of January 1815 — on the reading that the first of that act's two ages is hers.

name: Paolo Ventrice
source: Zambrone, Morti 1815, atto 40 — certified extract in Briatico, Matrimoni processetti 1849-1854
note: The deepest name on the bride's side, reached because his son's death act calls him «il fu Paolo». Husband of ANNA PAPPA.

name: Anna Pappa
source: Zambrone, Morti 1815, atto 40
note: Paolo Ventrice's wife, already dead when their son Domenico died in 1815.

name: Giuseppe Ventrice
bornNote: THIRTY-FOUR at his marriage on 2 March 1824, so born about 1790 -- AND BORN AT S. COSTANTINO, not Zambrone, which is the first birthplace this archive has had for him. HIS TWO DECLARED AGES DISAGREE: thirty-four in March 1824 gives 1790, and thirty-three in June 1828 gives 1795. Both are his own statements. The earlier one is preferred here only because it is the earlier one.
source: Zambrone, Matrimoni 1824, atto 2; Briatico, Nati 1828; Briatico, Morti 1831, atto 12
note: Giovanna's father, and he died TWO DAYS BEFORE HER THIRD BIRTHDAY. Act 12 of Briatico Morti 1831, read in the original: dead at two in the morning on 21 June 1831 in his own house, «di anni TRENTA», declared by Giacomo Comerci, a miller, and Rosario Zungri, a bracciale. THE YEAR CORRECTS THIS ARCHIVE: the certified copy in the marriage bundle was read as 1839 and published that way; the original says 1831 and the rest of the 1839 register agrees it cannot be. HIS AGE IS STILL IN DISPUTE — thirty at death (born c. 1801) against the thirty-three he gave for HIMSELF when he registered Giovanna's birth in June 1828 (born c. 1795). The archive carries his own declaration and keeps the other on the record. HE MARRIED AT ZAMBRONE ON 2 MARCH 1824, a contadino of thirty-four born at S. COSTANTINO, and the act calls him «figlio DEL FU DOMENICO e DELLA FU ANNA MAROPOLI» -- so BOTH HIS PARENTS WERE DEAD by then, which dates his mother's death for the first time. On the surname MAROPOLI against this archive's ANNA FAMA, see the corrections page.

name: Francesco Crupi
source: Queensland death registrations 1973/B/38514, 1961/B/45635, 1982/52783, 1989/57278
note: ANGELA CRUPI'S FATHER. Named only because his children's Queensland death registrations name him -- and as of today there are FOUR of them, not one. Angela (d. 1973), PIETRO (d. 1961), ANTONINO (d. 1982) and MARIO (d. 1989) all register the same two parents, FRANCESCO CRUPI and MARIA VECCHIO. A whole Sicilian sibling group in Brisbane, of which this archive knew one. Not in the family tree.

name: Maria Vecchio
source: Queensland death registrations 1973/B/38514, 1961/B/45635, 1982/52783, 1989/57278
note: ANGELA CRUPI'S MOTHER, and named in FOUR of her children's Queensland death registrations -- Angela's, Pietro's, Antonino's and Mario's. Not in the family tree.

name: Santa Donato (b. 1845, of Domenico Donato and Nunziata Sofi)
bornNote: Born at four o’clock at night on the 27th («ventisette andante») of November 1845 (Scilla, Nati 1845, atto 194, an_ua2002883, image 103, left page, read at the image by a delegated reader and read again by this session). The day of the act itself is overwritten in the heading, and the annual index (image 116, left page, no. 68) may read 29; the act’s own «ventisette» is what is held here, and the day is not certain.
source: Scilla, Nati 1845, atto 194 (an_ua2002883, image 103); annual index of 1845 (image 116, no. 68)
note: A DAUGHTER OF DOMENICO DONATO AND NUNZIATA SOFI, THE FIRST CHILD OF THEIRS YET FOUND, about a year after the parents’ marriage of 1844 (the next known are Candeloro, c. 1847, and Pasquale, 1849). The act: the midwife Teresa (surname not settled), fifty-four, declared that the child was born to Annunziata Sofi, filatrice, the lawful wife of Domenico Donato, thirty, marinaro, and gave the name Santa Donato; the witnesses were Francesco Principato (an esattore, the word is faint) and Giuseppe Fava, a barbiere, who signs. THE NAME IS SIGNIFICANT: Santa is the name of Domenico’s own mother, Santa Paladino (see Marta Paladino, whose given name is read Santa at the image), so the first daughter was named for the paternal grandmother, in the usual way. Domenico’s age is given as thirty, which is a year or so older than the December 1816 birth would make him (28 or 29), and the mother’s age is not safely read. A different Santa Donato was born in 1895 and another in 1900 to Michele Donato and Maria Sofi, a generation down; no death for the 1845 Santa has been looked for, and she is not to be confused with them.

name: Candeloro Donato (b. 1847)
bornNote: Aged twenty-seven at his marriage on 11 December 1874. Scilla.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1874, atto 62
note: MICHELE DONATO'S ELDER BROTHER, and named for the grandfather who has his own row above, and new to this archive. Married DOMENICA ROMANO, 21, a spinner, at Scilla on 11 December 1874. He was a sailor like his father, and unmarried before it. His existence is what the naming custom predicted: Domenico Donato was «figlio di Candeloro», so his first son should be a Candeloro, and here he is.

name: Domenica Romano
bornNote: Aged twenty-one at her marriage in December 1874. Scilla.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1874, atto 62
note: Candeloro Donato's wife. Not in the family tree.

name: Marta Paladino
bornNote: THIRTY when her son Domenico was born in December 1816.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845, fascicolo 20 (Nati 1816 atto 207; Nati 1818 atto 129); Matrimoni 1844, Tavola entry 17; Matrimoni 1845, atto 31
note: CANDELORO DONATO'S WIFE. HER GIVEN NAME IS IN DISPUTE AND THE DISPUTE IS WORTH KEEPING. Her son's birth act of 18 December 1816, written while she was in the next room, reads «e da MAR-TA PALADINO, di anni trenta, sua moglie legittima» -- the name broken across a line, and the second line beginning plainly «ta». The 1844 marriage Tavola calls her «Paladino MARIA». The act is contemporaneous and primary and the Tavola is an index made up at the year's end, and THIS VERY INDEX SERIES HAS ALREADY BEEN CAUGHT GIVING A MOTHER THE WRONG NAME -- the 1854 Tavola calls Serafina Arlotta «Rosa», and that error briefly made a brother into a cousin. Against that: the same 1844 Tavola gets the OTHER mother in the same entry exactly right, «de Amico Maria», as her own daughter's birth act confirms. So the index is not uniformly careless. MARTA is published here because the act says it; MARIA is recorded because the index says it. Another child of Candeloro in the Scilla births of 1810-1830 would settle it. UPDATE 18 NOVEMBER 2026, A CORRECTION OF THE READING ABOVE: re-zoomed at the image, act 207 of Nati 1816 (an_ua2002801, image 108) reads «e da SANTA Paladino, d'anni trenta, sua Moglie Legittima, Uno Maschio» with the name whole on one line and the capital a large looped S, so the «MAR-TA broken across a line» reading is withdrawn. Santa is now the reading of the 1816 act itself and of the indexes of 1818, 1823 and 1824 and the 1823 act; Maria and Marta are the 1844 Tavola's and the earlier reading's. The row keeps the name Marta Paladino until the name is changed for every page that links to it, which is a decision, not a correction. UPDATE 22 NOVEMBER 2026, THE 1844 TAVOLA IS ALSO SANTA: the Matrimoni 1844 Tavola (an_ua2002588, image 50, entry 17) was zoomed again at the image and reads «Candeloro e Paladino Santa» for the groom’s parents, with the bride’s «Pasquale e De Amico Maria» below, so the earlier statement above that the Tavola calls her «Maria» was a misreading of that line and is withdrawn. Every reading at the image now agrees on Santa: the act of 1816, the acts of 1818 (atto 62) and 1823, the indexes of 1818, 1823 and 1824, and the Tavola of 1844. Only the first reading of the 1816 act, now withdrawn, ever read Marta. The row still carries the name Marta Paladino until David decides to rename it for every page that links to it.

name: Pasquale Sofi
bornNote: BAPTISED 4 JUNE 1786 (a Latin extract of 17 August 1816 in the marriage bundle of 1816, Scilla processetti an_ua2093354, fascicolo 1816 n. 20, image 268, read at the image on 22 Nov 2026: «hodie natum ex Rocco Sofi et Nuntia Galli conjugibus», named Pascalis Franciscus Bruno, the godfather Bruno Cosentino). Thirty at his marriage in 1816, which agrees; the birth act of November 1818 gives him thirty-eight, which the baptism shows to be six years too many (he was thirty-two).
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845, fascicolo 20 (Nati 1816 atto 207; Nati 1818 atto 129); Scilla, Matrimoni 1816, atto 20 (an_ua2002512, images 23-24, read at the image); Scilla, Morti 1873 atto 89 (an_ua16601185, image 19, read at the image); Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1816 (an_ua2093354, image 268)
note: NUNZIATA SOFI'S FATHER, and a sailor like the Donato men he married into. Alive in July 1844: his daughter's marriage bundle holds no death certificate for him. Not in the family tree. 17 NOV 2026 -- HIS MARRIAGE AND HIS PARENTS. Scilla Matrimoni 1816 atto 20: on 29 August 1816 PASQUALE SOFI, marinaro, eldest son of ROCCO SOFI (62, also a marinaro) and NUNZIA GALLI (56), both present and consenting, promises marriage to MARIA D'AMICO (25, a filatrice), eldest daughter of the late Rocco d'Amico, who died at Pistone in Sicily on 2 December 1808, and of Angela di Tuzzo (50; the surname reading is uncertain); publications 18 and 25 August; the groom signs «Pascale Sofi»; the foot note says they were married by the parish priest of Scilla in early September 1816 (the day word is doubtful). His age is overwritten in the act and reads thirty, against thirty-eight in 1818 and the forty-three or forty-four of 1827-34: ages in these acts are loose. Nothing here says he is or is not the Pasquale Sofi of the tree. UPDATE 18 NOVEMBER 2026, HIS DEATH: Scilla Morti 1873 atto 89 (read at the image): «PASQUALE SOFI, dei furono Rocco ed Annunziata D'Pasquale (the surname is doubtful), marito di Maria D'Amico», about eighty-seven, a PESCATORE, died at 7 a.m. on 3 July 1873 in his own house in the rione Acquagrande, declared by two bidelli. His age is the act's and agrees with the 1816-27 acts only loosely (about 83 by the 1827 birth act); the mother is written Annunziata here and Nunzia Galli in his 1816 marriage promise, so the act's second name is not relied on.

name: Maria de Amico
bornNote: BAPTISED 16 OCTOBER 1791, named Maria Antonia Giuseppa (a Latin extract of 17 August 1816 in the marriage bundle, Scilla processetti an_ua2093354, fascicolo 1816 n. 20, image 269, read at the image on 22 Nov 2026: «natam ex Rocco de Amico et Angela de Zarro conjugibus»; the mother's surname is written de Zarro here and di Tuzzo in the marriage act, and the reading of either is doubtful). Twenty-five at her marriage in 1816 agrees; the birth act of November 1818 gives her twenty-five, which the baptism shows to be two years too few (she was twenty-seven).
died: November 1873, at Scilla (Morti 1873 atto 163; the day is not securely read)
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845, fascicolo 20 (Nati 1816 atto 207; Nati 1818 atto 129); Matrimoni 1844, Tavola entry 17; Scilla, Matrimoni 1816, atto 20 (an_ua2002512, images 23-24, read at the image); Scilla, Morti 1873 atto 163 (an_ua16601185, images 32-33, read by a delegated reader); Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1816 (an_ua2093354, image 269)
note: Nunziata Sofi's mother. Not in the family tree. HER NAME IS CONFIRMED TWICE, by her daughter's birth act of 1818 and by the 1844 Tavola independently, which is why the Tavola's reading of the OTHER mother in the same entry is a question rather than a verdict -- see [[Marta Paladino]]. NOTE A COINCIDENCE, NOT A JOIN: the Michele Donato of act 31 of 1845 married an ANGELA DE AMICO. De Amico is common at Scilla and nothing yet connects the two women. 17 NOV 2026 -- HER PARENTS AND HER MARRIAGE: married Pasquale Sofi at Scilla on 29 August 1816 (promise; Matrimoni 1816 atto 20), aged TWENTY-FIVE, a filatrice, the eldest daughter of the late Rocco d'Amico (died at Pistone in Sicily, 2 December 1808, the act says, quoting the death act of that comune) and of Angela di Tuzzo, fifty. Her age here (25 in 1816) and in 1818 (25) is the same number twice: one of the two is loose. The Michele Donato who married an ANGELA DE AMICO in 1845 is still only a coincidence of surnames. UPDATE 18 NOVEMBER 2026, HER DEATH: Scilla Morti 1873 atto 163 (read by a delegated reader at the image, the day and month partly read): «dei furono Rocco e Mariangela Tuzzo?, vedova di Sofi Pasquale, ottantasette circa», a filatrice, died in November 1873, four months after her husband. Her mother is written Mariangela Tuzzo here and Angela di Tuzzo in the 1816 promise: the same name in two hands.

name: Rocco Sofi
bornNote: SIXTY-TWO at his son Pasquale's marriage promise of 29 August 1816 (Scilla, Matrimoni 1816, atto 20).
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1816, atto 20 (an_ua2002512, images 23-24, read at the image)
note: PASQUALE SOFI'S FATHER, alive and present in August 1816, a sailor like his son. Not in the family tree. His wife is Nunzia Galli.

name: Nunzia Galli
bornNote: FIFTY-SIX at her son Pasquale's marriage promise of 29 August 1816 (Scilla, Matrimoni 1816, atto 20).
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1816, atto 20 (an_ua2002512, images 23-24, read at the image)
note: PASQUALE SOFI'S MOTHER, alive and present in August 1816, wife of Rocco Sofi. Not in the family tree.

name: Rocco d'Amico
bornNote: Named only as the late father of Maria d'Amico, the bride of 29 August 1816 (Scilla, Matrimoni 1816, atto 20).
died: 2 December 1808, at Pistone in Sicily (as the marriage act quotes the death act of that comune)
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1816, atto 20 (an_ua2002512, images 23-24, read at the image)
note: MARIA D'AMICO'S FATHER; he died in Sicily in 1808 while the family lived at Scilla, which is the reason the act records where and when. He is placed at Scilla only because his daughter married there; Pistone in Sicily, where he died, is not a place this archive maps and has not been identified. Not in the family tree.

name: Angela di Tuzzo
bornNote: FIFTY at her daughter Maria's marriage promise of 29 August 1816 (Scilla, Matrimoni 1816, atto 20); the surname reads di Tuzzo or di Duzzo and is not settled.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1816, atto 20 (an_ua2002512, images 23-24, read at the image)
note: MARIA D'AMICO'S MOTHER, alive and present in August 1816, widow of Rocco d'Amico. A Caterina d'Amico, daughter of a Rocco d'Amico and an Angela di Tuzzo (Matrimoni 1816 atto 5, married Fortunato Catalano), is probably Maria's sister. Not in the family tree.

name: Carmine Donato (b. c. 1805, of Candeloro Donato and Giovanna Vita)
bornNote: TWENTY-TWO at the marriage promise of 22 November 1827 (Scilla, Matrimoni 1827, atto 22), born at Scilla.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1827, atto 22 (an_ua2002542, images 25-26, read at the image)
note: A DONATO WHO IS NOT MICHELE'S LINE, so far as anything shows: son of the LATE Candeloro Donato and Giovanna Vita, whereas Michele Donato's grandfather Candeloro (b. c. 1783, wife Marta Paladino) was alive in 1844-45. Married Nunziata Sofi (26, born at Scilla, daughter of the late Domenico Sofi and Angela Longordo) on 30 November 1827; the celebration witnesses were D. Rocco Chilinge? and Gennaro Sofi. His sister Candida (daughter of the late Candeloro Donato and Giovanna Vita) married Domenico Vita on 15 September 1834 (Matrimoni 1834 atto 28, not read here). Not in the family tree.

name: Annunziata Sofi (b. c. 1801, of Domenico Sofi and Angela Longordo)
bornNote: TWENTY-SIX at the marriage promise of 22 November 1827 (Scilla, Matrimoni 1827, atto 22), born at Scilla.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1827, atto 22 (an_ua2002542, images 25-26, read at the image)
note: A SECOND NUNZIATA SOFI AT SCILLA, TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE with the same name, and not Michele Donato's mother (who was born in November 1818 to Pasquale Sofi and Maria d'Amico and was nine years old in 1827). This one, a daughter of the late Domenico Sofi and Angela Longordo, married the sailor Carmine Donato on 30 November 1827; any Donato-Sofi child of 1828-38 may be hers, so a Sofi mother of that period is not to be taken for the Pasquale Sofi line without the father's name. Not in the family tree.

name: Michele Donato (b. Messina, c. 1814)
bornNote: Thirty-one at his marriage in August 1845, and the act says NATO IN MESSINA — the only member of this family so far recorded as born across the strait, in Sicily rather than Calabria.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1845, atto 31
note: DOMENICO DONATO'S ELDER BROTHER, and NOT THE MICHELE DONATO OF THIS ARCHIVE'S SPINE. Two men of the name stand three feet apart in these records: this one, born about 1814 at Messina, and his nephew born at Scilla on 3 October 1855 and named for him. Keep them apart. His act is what dates the grandfather — «FIGLIO DI Candeloro Donato», not «del fu», so CANDELORO WAS STILL ALIVE in August 1845 — and it is his mother's surname, PALADINO, that the 1844 Tavola then matched to make the brothers brothers.

name: Angela de Amico
bornNote: Thirty-two at her marriage in August 1845.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1845, atto 31
note: Michele Donato of Messina's wife. Not in the family tree. A COINCIDENCE AND NOT A JOIN: her husband's brother Domenico had married a Sofi whose own mother was a MARIA DE AMICO the year before. De Amico is common at Scilla and nothing yet connects the two women — but two de Amico women marrying into one Donato household in successive years is worth a look when the Scilla births of the 1810s are read.

name: Francesco Cichello
bornNote: Not yet sought. Zambrone's registers begin in 1811, so unless he outlived that he is pre-civil.
source: Zambrone, Matrimoni 1824, atto 2
note: CATERINA CICHELLO'S FATHER, named in his daughter's marriage act of 2 March 1824 as «il fu Francesco» -- already dead. Entirely new to this archive, and one of the two people row 34 of the work list existed to find. Not in the family tree.

name: Vittoria Mollo
bornNote: Not yet sought.
source: Zambrone, Matrimoni 1824, atto 2
note: CATERINA CICHELLO'S MOTHER, «la fu Vittoria Mollo» in her daughter's marriage act of 1824. Entirely new. NOTE THE SURNAME: a MOLLO appears twice more in the Zambrone marriages of these years -- Pasquale Piatto's mother is an Anna Mollo in 1823 -- so the Mollo were a Zambrone family and she was probably local.

name: Pietro Crupi
bornNote: Entered as born 1898 on the Brisbane aliens register of 1930, NAA: BP9/3 ITALIAN CRUPI P.
source: Queensland death registrations 1961/B/45635, 1982/52783, 1989/57278; NAA: BP9/3 ITALIAN CRUPI P; NAA: BP4/3 ITALIAN CRUPI P
note: ANGELA CRUPI'S BROTHER, and new to this archive. His Queensland death registration of 1961 names FRANCESCO CRUPI and MARIA VECCHIO -- the same parents as hers. Angela married Rosario Mazza and lies at Nudgee; her brothers were in Queensland too, and nobody here knew it. HE CAME WITH ANTONINO. Both brothers arrived in Brisbane on the OTRANTO on 19 AUGUST 1930, Pietro entered as born 1898 and Antonino as born 1907. AND HE HAS NO ALIENS CARD FOR A REASON: NAA: BP4/3 ITALIAN CRUPI P records «Alien Registration Certificate NOT ISSUED», the folio noting that he was NATURALISED 23 FEBRUARY 1932. By 1939 he was a British subject and outside the series. The absence is explained, not unexplained.

name: Antonino Crupi
bornNote: His own aliens registration card, NAA D4028 item 9209610, registered at Ingham police station on 3 October 1939: birthplace Piedimonte Etneo, date of birth 5.10.07.
source: Queensland death registrations 1961/B/45635, 1982/52783, 1989/57278; NAA: D4028, CRUPI ANTONIO (item 9209610) read in full; NAA: A714 57/18792; NAA: BP9/3 ITALIAN CRUPI A
note: A SECOND BROTHER OF ANGELA CRUPI, same parents on the registration. An Antonino Crupi marries in Queensland on 24 August 1940, very likely him. READ IN FULL 20 SEPTEMBER. Born 5 OCTOBER 1907 at PIEDIMONTE ETNEO -- the Mazza's own town, like his brother Mario. A BOOT REPAIRER at Ingham, Box 484, Abbott Street. Entered Australia 2 SEPTEMBER 1930, port of debarkation BRISBANE; he and his brother PIETRO came on the OTRANTO, which reached Brisbane on 19 August 1930. Five feet four, black eyes, black hair, sturdy build, THE FOURTH FINGER OF HIS RIGHT HAND DEFORMED. Entered as MARRIED in October 1939. HE WAS INTERNED: the card is stamped LOVEDAY 35924, the reverse records him moved «ex Gay[thorne] to 14A» on 16 March 1943 and RELEASED AND RETURNED TO QUEENSLAND ON 22 OCTOBER 1943. Naturalised 7 November 1946, then at TULLY, wife NELLIE.

name: Mario Crupi
bornNote: Not yet sought. Sicilian-born, like his sister, who was born at Catania in 1900.
source: Queensland death registrations 1961/B/45635, 1982/52783, 1989/57278
note: A THIRD BROTHER OF ANGELA CRUPI, same parents again. A «Mariano Crupi» marries on 31 January 1940 -- the two names are interchangeable in this index.

name: Gennaro Melluso
bornNote: Not yet sought.
source: Queensland death registrations 1971/C/6628 and 1991/9389
note: GREGORIO MELLUSO'S FATHER. NOT A NEW FINDING -- his son's Queensland death registration of 1971 has been in `data/qld-bdm.tsv` for days. What is new is that he is now a PERSON here rather than a cell in a spreadsheet, which is the only way he reaches the reader. Not in the family tree.

name: Maria Limardo
bornNote: Not yet sought.
source: Queensland death registrations 1971/C/6628 and 1991/9389
note: GREGORIO MELLUSO'S MOTHER, from the same registration and likewise already recorded, never surfaced. LIMARDO IS A POTENZONI SURNAME -- it appears in the Potenzoni birth index of 1818 -- which places this Melluso household in the Briatico-Potenzoni district rather than among the Agrigento Melluso that fill Geneanet. Not in the family tree.

name: Carmela Maria Borello
bornNote: Not yet sought.
source: Queensland death registrations 1971/C/6628 and 1991/9389
note: MARIA ASSUNTA'S MOTHER and GREGORIO MELLUSO'S WIFE, named in her daughter's registration of 1991 and held in `qld-bdm.tsv` without ever becoming a person. NOTE A NAME ALREADY IN THE TREE, AND NOTHING MORE THAN A NOTE: the export contains a COSIMO BORELLO. Borello is not rare and no record connects them.

name: Gregorio Melluso
bornNote: From his grave at Mareeba New Cemetery.
source: Queensland death registration 1971/C/6628; Mareeba New Cemetery
note: BURIED AT MAREEBA, in far north Queensland -- Section 4 Catholic, Row I, Plot 10 -- a long way from the Brisbane the rest of this family settled in, and his registration is marked C for a country event. His parents GENNARO MELLUSO and MARIA LIMARDO come from that registration, which this archive has held since before today; what it lacked was the people.

name: Maria Assunta Melluso
bornNote: Fifty-five at her death in October 1991.
source: Queensland death registration 1991/9389; Mount Gravatt Cemetery
note: THE FIRST PROSTAMO EVER FOUND IN THE QUEENSLAND INDEX, and she was born a MELLUSO. She is buried at Mount Gravatt as MARIA ASSUNTA PROSTAMO in plot 3B-607, immediately beside DOMENICO FRANCESCO PROSTAMO in 3B-608 -- husband and wife by the adjacent-plot rule. A MELLUSO MARRIED A PROSTAMO A SECOND TIME, two generations after Alfonso Prostamo married Caterina Melluso at Briatico on 21 May 1887; HOW SHE JOINS ALFONSO'S LINE IS UNTESTED and a repeated surname pairing is a hint, not a descent. Trove has her independently, naturalised 4 July 1966 at 3 Frank Street, Graceville. THE TWO DATES RECONCILE: she DIED on 27 October 1991 and was BURIED on the 30th.

name: Generosa Costa
bornNote: Not yet sought. Her age is lost under an ink blot in her own marriage act.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1888, atto 63
note: ROCCO ARENA'S WIFE, and SHE IS IN THE FAMILY TREE -- this row exists only to connect her to parents the tree does not have. Her marriage act of December 1888 reads «COSTA GENEROSA, FILATRICE, nata in Scilla, FIGLIA DI ANTONIO, residente in Scilla, E DI ANNA ARLOTTA, residente in Scilla». Both parents were recorded in this archive as documented people and NEITHER WAS CONNECTED TO HER, so no chart and no page could show that Rocco Arena's wife had known parents. That is the same failure as the five Melluso who sat in a spreadsheet column: a fact held in one file does not reach the reader until it is joined to another.

name: Antonio Arena (b. New York 1896)
bornNote: Exact, from his baptism transcript. BORN IN MANHATTAN, not at Scilla — the first member of this family documented as born outside Italy.
source: New York Roman Catholic Parish Baptisms — Our Lady of Loretto, 15 November 1896 (Findmypast US/NY/CATH/PR/BAP/01052845)
note: ROCCO ARENA AND GENEROSA COSTA'S SON, BORN IN NEW YORK. Baptised at OUR LADY OF LORETTO on 15 November 1896, six weeks old, with the family at 141 MULBERRY STREET. THE TREE HAS AN «Antonio Arena» AMONG ROCCO'S CHILDREN AND NO DATES FOR HIM; this is very probably the same boy, but the export's Antonio carries nothing to test it against, so he is entered here rather than merged. HIS BIRTH DATES THE EMIGRATION FROM THE INSIDE: his sister Anna was born at Scilla in January 1893 and he was born in Manhattan in October 1896, so the household crossed between those two dates -- which fits the 1892 and 1894 crossings already documented for his father.

name: Serafina Arena (b. New York 1898)
bornNote: Exact, from her baptism transcript. BORN IN MANHATTAN. Baptised at Our Lady of Loretto on 18 September 1898, the family at 141 MULBERRY STREET.
source: New York Roman Catholic Parish Baptisms, Our Lady of Loretto and Most Precious Blood (Findmypast) — US/NY/CATH/PR/BAP/01054593
note: ROCCO ARENA AND GENEROSA COSTA'S SECOND NEW YORK CHILD, and not in the family tree. Named SERAFINA — which is her paternal grandmother's name, SERAFINA ARLOTTA, exactly as Calabrian custom prescribes for a first daughter born after the family's own Anna. The naming custom followed them across the Atlantic.

name: Clementina Arena (b. New York 1900)
bornNote: Exact, from her baptism transcript. Baptised at Our Lady of Loretto on 20 January 1901, the family now at 198 MULBERRY STREET.
source: New York Roman Catholic Parish Baptisms, Our Lady of Loretto and Most Precious Blood (Findmypast) — US/NY/CATH/PR/BAP/01057021
note: THE THIRD NEW YORK CHILD, and not in the family tree. HER RECORD MOVES THE HOUSEHOLD: her two elder siblings were baptised from 141 Mulberry and she from 198 MULBERRY, so the family shifted along the same street between 1898 and 1900.

name: Antonio Arena (b. New York 1902)
bornNote: Exact, from his baptism transcript. Baptised at MOST PRECIOUS BLOOD, Manhattan, on 2 November 1902 — a different parish from his three elder siblings.
source: New York Roman Catholic Parish Baptisms, Our Lady of Loretto and Most Precious Blood (Findmypast) — US/NY/CATH/PR/BAP/PH2/00198880
note: THE SECOND ANTONIO, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Rocco Arena and Generosa Costa baptised a son ANTONIO on 15 November 1896 and another son ANTONIO on 2 November 1902. IN THIS FAMILY'S PRACTICE THAT MEANS THE FIRST CHILD DIED and the name was given again -- the same reading this archive already made of ORAZIO ARENA'S TWO SONS NAMED DOMENICO at Scilla in 1856 and 1859. The export holds one «Antonio Arena» among Rocco's children with no dates. IT IS PROBABLY THIS ONE, the survivor, but nothing in the export can test that, so both are recorded here and neither is merged. HIS MOTHER IS TRANSCRIBED «GENEROSA COLTA» -- one more of this data's garblings, beside Lecota for Nicotra, Postamo for Prostamo and Cupo for Crupi.

name: Giuseppe Polistena
bornNote: THIRTY-EIGHT when his daughter Annunziata was born on 2 December 1836, so born about 1798.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 19 October 1924 (Camillo Antonio Polistena); Scilla, Nati 1836 atto 204
note: A NEW ANCESTOR ON THE THINNEST QUARTER. Named as Camillo Antonio Polistena's father on his death act. The Polistena quarter had NO documented ancestor above Camillo Antonio at all; this is the first, and his wife Anna Pontillo is the second. DATED AND GIVEN A TRADE: thirty-eight and a MARINARO in December 1836. That sets the Polistena beside the Arena and the Arlotta as another Scilla sailing family, and it is the first fact about him that is not a name on his son's death act. AND A DEATH BOUND AT LAST: «il FU Giuseppe» and «la FU Anna Pontillo» in their son Camillo Antonio's marriage act of 23 JANUARY 1881, each «residente in vita in Scilla». Both were alive at their daughter Fortunata's birth in January 1840 and dead by January 1881. A THIRD AGE, AND IT DOES NOT AGREE: he is FIFTY in September 1844 (Nati 1844 atto 137), against thirty-eight in December 1836 and thirty-four in December 1833. Births of 1794, 1798 and 1799. The two earlier figures agree with each other and this one does not; recorded, not averaged.

name: Anna Pontillo
bornNote: THIRTY-FIVE when her daughter Annunziata was born on 2 December 1836, so born about 1801.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 19 October 1924 (Camillo Antonio Polistena); Scilla, Nati 1836 atto 204
note: CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA'S MOTHER, AND THE SOLUTION TO THE PONTILLO PROBLEM. The tree calls Giovanni Polistena's mother «Giovanna Pontillo». Three records call her Giovanna ROMANO. Here is where the Pontillo came from: it is the surname of Giovanni's PATERNAL GRANDMOTHER, one generation up, carried down onto the wrong woman. AND THE ACT OF 1836 CONFIRMS HER SURNAME AGAINST AN INDEX THAT GOT IT WRONG: the annual Tavola enters her daughter as «di Giuseppe e MARTELLO Anna»; the act says PONTILLO, which is what the death act of 1924 says too. AND A DEATH BOUND AT LAST: «il FU Giuseppe» and «la FU Anna Pontillo» in their son Camillo Antonio's marriage act of 23 JANUARY 1881, each «residente in vita in Scilla». Both were alive at their daughter Fortunata's birth in January 1840 and dead by January 1881.

name: Pasquale Donato
bornNote: Born at eight in the morning on 27 May 1860 (Scilla, Nati 1860 atto 98, read at the image); registered the next day.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 20 April 1937; Scilla, Nati 1860 atto 98, read in the original (an_ua2002931, image 52)
note: THE CHILD THE NAMING CUSTOM PREDICTED, FOUND. Row 4 of the work list reasoned that Domenico Donato and Nunziata Sofi should have a PASQUALE for the maternal grandfather Pasquale Sofi. Here he is, with both parents named on his death act, and a wife: GENEROSA COSTA. UPDATE 17 NOVEMBER 2026: HIS BIRTH ACT, and the naming prediction was right to the day it was made: Pasquale, born at Scilla on 27 May 1860 to Domenico Donato, a marinaio, and Annunziata Sofi (the act's ages are 32 for each, which cannot be right for a man born in 1816: the ages in these acts are not relied on); declared by the midwife Giuseppa de Girolamo, the witnesses Epifanio d'Amico and Giuseppe Idone. He died at seventy-six on 20 April 1937. A PASQUALE born in 1849 to a Domenico Donato (the index reads the mother Sofi Lucia?, an Annunziata misread, and the act was not opened) is probably an earlier Pasquale who died young, since the name was given again in 1860; not claimed. UPDATE 18 NOVEMBER 2026: the 1849 Pasquale is found and read (see Pasquale Donato b. 1849): born 5 October 1849, act 186, mother written Nun?iata Sofi. He is therefore an earlier child of the same two parents, and the name was given again in 1860, which suggests he died young; no death act has been looked for.

name: Pasquale Donato (b. 1849, of Domenico Donato and Nunziata Sofi)
bornNote: Born at five o'clock on 5 October 1849 (Scilla, Nati 1849 atto 186, an_ua2002893, image 96, read at the image by a delegated reader); the act was registered at two in the afternoon of the same day before the sindaco Gaetano Ferrante, and the baptism column says baptised 6 October. The annual index gave the day as 3: the act says 5.
source: Scilla, Nati 1849 atto 186 (an_ua2002893, image 96); annual index of 1849 (an_ua2002896, image 28)
note: A SON OF DOMENICO DONATO AND NUNZIATA SOFI AND AN EARLIER PASQUALE THAN THE ONE OF 1860, TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE WITH ONE NAME in one family: the name Pasquale (for the maternal grandfather Pasquale Sofi) was given in 1849 and again in 1860, which is the usual sign that the first child had died. The act: father Domenico Donato, 35, marinaro, who declared the birth; mother Nun?iata Sofi, 28 (the fourth letter is a looped z or d, so Nunziata), his lawful wife; witnesses a barber and a shoemaker named Martello or Maltella (the first surname doubtful). The index line read the mother as Sofi Lucia or Lunziata and the day as 3; both were misreadings of this hand. No death for him has been looked for, and his burial is not claimed.

name: Domenico Arlotta (d. 1915)
bornNote: Seventy-three when he died on 14 March 1915, so born about 1842. Rione Chianalea, Scilla.
source: Scilla, Morti 1915, parte I, atto 34 — read in the original
note: SERAFINA ARLOTTA'S BROTHER, and the act names both their parents: «da fu GIOVANNI e da fu COSTA MARIA». A MARINARO, husband of MARIA PONTILLO, dead at noon on 14 March 1915 at the RIONE CHIANALEA. He carries his grandfather's name -- the DOMENICO ARLOTTA this archive knows only from «figlio del fu Domenico» in an 1854 birth act -- which is what the naming custom predicts and is not proof of him.

name: Anna Arlotta (Serafina's sister)
bornNote: Eighty when she died on 16 March 1915, so born about 1835 — five years after her sister Serafina, who was born 13 June 1830.
source: Scilla, Morti 1915, parte I, atto 36 — read in the original
note: SERAFINA ARLOTTA'S SISTER AND GENEROSA COSTA'S MOTHER, and the act settles both at once: «e morta ARLOTTA ANNA, di anni OTTANTA, casalinga ... da fu GIOVANNI e da fu COSTA MARIA, MOGLIE DI COSTA ANTONINO». Those are Serafina Arlotta's own parents and Generosa Costa's own father. SHE DIED AT FOUR IN THE MORNING ON 16 MARCH 1915 at the QUARTIERE CHIANALEA, two days after her brother Domenico and eleven weeks before her husband.

name: Giuseppe Antonio Arlotta
bornNote: Not yet sought. A brother of Serafina Arlotta.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 2 June 1918
note: A THIRD CHILD OF GIOVANNI ARLOTTA AND MARIA COSTA, husband of ANGELA NUNZIATA PIZZARELLO. Serafina Arlotta was an only child in this archive until today; she now has three documented siblings.

name: Lorenzo Costa
bornNote: Not yet sought. Father of Antonino Costa, who died at Scilla on 1 June 1915, so a birth in the 1810s or 1820s — inside Scilla's civil run, which begins in 1809.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 1 June 1915 (Antonio Costa)
note: GENEROSA COSTA'S PATERNAL GRANDFATHER, named on her father's death act. He is a generation above anything this archive held on the Costa side, which until today stopped at Antonio Costa «b. c. 1840».

name: Generosa Polistena
bornNote: Not yet sought.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 1 June 1915 (Antonio Costa)
note: GENEROSA COSTA'S PATERNAL GRANDMOTHER — AND THE REASON FOR HER NAME. Southern Italian custom gives the first daughter her paternal grandmother's name, and Generosa Costa, who married Rocco Arena in December 1888, carries this woman's exactly. IT ALSO PUTS A POLISTENA INSIDE THE COSTA LINE a generation before the Polistena quarter's own marriages, which is worth noticing in a town where four of this family's quarters keep intermarrying.

name: Annunziato Romano
bornNote: Not yet sought. Father of Giovanna Romano, who died at Scilla on 15 July 1930, so a birth in the 1820s or 1830s — inside Scilla's civil run.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 15 July 1930 (Giovanna Romano)
note: GIOVANNI POLISTENA'S MATERNAL GRANDFATHER, and a name this archive could never have found because it was looking for a PONTILLO. He is named on his daughter's own death act.

name: Angela Zirilli
bornNote: Not yet sought.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 15 July 1930 (Giovanna Romano)
note: GIOVANNA ROMANO'S MOTHER. NOTE THE SURNAME: Orazio Arena's wife was GIOVANNA ZIRILLI, and here is an ANGELA ZIRILLI marrying into the Romano. TWO ZIRILLI WOMEN MARRYING INTO TWO OF THIS FAMILY'S FOUR QUARTERS, which in a town this size is more likely kinship than coincidence -- and is not yet evidence of it.

name: Serafina Arena (the infant of 1912)
bornNote: Three months old when she died on 15 August 1912, so born about the middle of May. Quartiere Chianalea, Scilla.
source: Scilla, Morti 1912, parte I, atto 83
note: A CHILD THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT KNOW EXISTED, found while trying to prove something else. Rocco Arena and Generosa Costa had a daughter SERAFINA born at Scilla about May 1912 who lived three months. SHE IS THE SECOND SERAFINA: the first was baptised at Our Lady of Loretto, Manhattan, on 15 August 1898, and the couple gave the name again in Calabria fourteen years later -- the same reading this archive makes of their TWO SONS NAMED ANTONIO. NOTE WHAT SHE PROVES INCIDENTALLY: the household was at Scilla and still having children in 1912, which is the return from America seen from the inside, and GENEROSA COSTA was bearing a child at about forty-four. Her father is «ROCCO, MARINARO» here and «PESCATORE» on his own death act of 1932.

name: Anna Barbaro
bornNote: SEVENTY-FIVE at her death on 2 February 1836 («di anni settantacinque», Scilla Morti 1836 atto 9, read at the image), so born about 1760 at Scilla («nata in questo Comune»); a stated age, so only about. Pre-civil: her baptism would be a parish record. The age fits Giovanni Arlotta as a son born about 1779 (the age-75 reading of 1854), when she was nineteen.
father: Domenico Varbaro (father of Anna Barbaro, d. before 1836)
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 28; Scilla, Morti 1823 atto 27; Scilla, Morti 1836 atto 9 (an_ua2002711, image 7, right page) and its Tavola (image 59, row 99)
note: GIOVANNI ARLOTTA'S MOTHER, and ALIVE at her son's wedding on 30 August 1828 -- «domiciliata ivi», where her husband is «fu». A name this archive has never held. She is Serafina Arlotta's grandmother and a great-great-great-great-great-grandmother of the two children. BARBARO is a Scilla surname in its own right -- an Antonio Barbaro marries there the following year. HER HUSBAND'S DEATH ACT NOW FOUND: Domenico Arlotta died 17 March 1823 aged ninety-five, «vedovo di Francesca Paladino, e marito di Anna Barbaro» (Morti 1823 atto 27, read at the image), so she was his second wife and a widow by 1823; the 1828 act's «domiciliata ivi» is hers. Her own age and parents are not given there. HER DEATH ACT FOUND AND READ AT THE IMAGE, 25 Nov 2026: Scilla Morti 1836 atto 9, 3 February 1836 at three in the afternoon, before the sindaco Giacomo Mirabile (reading of the surname uncertain): «Anna Varbaro, vedova di Domenico Arlotta», born in Scilla, aged seventy-five, «figlia del fu Domenico Varbaro» (her mother is not named, her profession and her father's profession are blank), died in her own house on 2 February at four o'clock. Declared by Pasquale Cantino (thirty, marinaro) and Giovanni Campanella (seventy-three, marinaro), both of Scilla. She is the Anna Barbaro of Giovanni Arlotta's marriage act (written Barbaro there, Varbaro in her own death act and in the Tavola, where she is filed under V). The Tavola entry, found first, gave the date and «Ved.a Dom.co Arlotta». Earlier years 1829-1835 (Tavola A/B and V pages only) hold no widow of Domenico Arlotta; the Varbaro Anna of 1833 is a child of living parents.

name: Domenico Varbaro (father of Anna Barbaro, d. before 1836)
bornNote: Not sought. Pre-civil.
source: Scilla, Morti 1836 atto 9 (an_ua2002711, image 7)
note: NAMED AS «fu Domenico Varbaro» in his daughter Anna Varbaro's death act of 2 February 1836, so dead by then. Nothing else is known of him: no trade, no wife, no age. The surname is written Varbaro in the act; the same woman is Barbaro in her son's marriage act. Not sought in the Scilla Morti before 1836 (the Tavolas of 1829-1835 were read only for his daughter).

name: Rocco Costa
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore a parish record.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 28
note: MARIA COSTA'S FATHER, a MARINARO, and he STOOD AT HER WEDDING on 30 August 1828 and gave his «espresso e formale consenso» in person. Not in the family tree. NOTE WHAT HE IS NOT: this archive briefly carried a DOMENICO COSTA, commerciante, as a candidate for Maria's father, on the strength of his standing witness at her daughter's registration in 1830. HER FATHER WAS ROCCO. The candidate is withdrawn by the act, which is what candidates are for.

name: Pasqualina Idone
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 28
note: MARIA COSTA'S MOTHER, alive and present at her daughter's wedding on 30 August 1828, consenting with her husband Rocco Costa. IDONE is a Scilla surname this archive has met once before -- a Giuseppe Idone, sixty-four, witnessed Rocco Arena's birth in 1861, thirty-three years later and four generations down the same street.

name: Candida Costa
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore a parish record.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1811, Tavola annuale
note: MARIA COSTA'S SISTER, and so SERAFINA ARLOTTA'S AUNT. She married GIOVANNI VILARDI at Scilla in 1811; the annual Tavola names her parents as «Rocco e Pasqualina Idone», the same couple who stood at Maria's wedding in August 1828 and gave their consent in person. Her husband's parents are GAETANO VILARDI and ANTONIA MELLICA. Not in the family tree. FOUND IN AN INDEX OPENED FOR SOMEBODY ELSE -- the 1811 Tavola was being read for Filippo Arena, who is not in it.

name: Annunziata Polistina
bornNote: Born at eight in the morning in her parents' own house, declared the same evening by the midwife Teresa Arena, forty-four.
source: Scilla, Nati 1836 atto 204
note: CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA'S SISTER, and the first sibling he has ever had in this archive. She was found through an index entry that named her mother WRONGLY -- «Martello Anna» where the act says ANNA PONTILLO -- and opening the act both corrected the index and confirmed the parentage that Camillo Antonio's own death act of 1924 gives. The surname is spelt POLISTINA in this act and POLISTENA in his; the register uses both.

name: Rocco Polistina
bornNote: Born at SIX IN THE MORNING on 13 December 1833 in his parents' own house, declared two days later by the midwife TERESA ARENA, thirty-eight.
source: Scilla, Nati 1833 atto 174, read in the original
note: A SECOND SIBLING OF CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA, three years older than Annunziata. The index spells the mother PONTILLO here, correctly -- the same index got her wrong three years later, which is a useful reminder that an index can be right and wrong about the same woman in the same series. HIS ACT IS ATTO 174 AND IT HAS BEEN READ. It gives his parents' ages -- Giuseppe thirty-four and a MARINARO, Anna thirty-three -- which cross-check his sister's act of 1836 exactly. AND ITS MARGIN CARRIES HIS MARRIAGE: «L'anno 1869, il giorno 12 Luglio ... ha contratto matrimonio in questo Comune con COLORINA BRI[...]». He lived to thirty-five and married at Scilla on 12 JULY 1869; the bride's name is cut by the binding and is recorded as read, uncertain. Not in the family tree.

name: Fortunata Polistina
bornNote: Given in the 1840 annual birth Tavola, entry 107, which names her parents «Giuse. e Pontillo Anna».
source: Scilla, Nati 1840, Tavola annuale, entry 107
note: A THIRD CHILD OF GIUSEPPE POLISTENA AND ANNA PONTILLO, and so a third sibling of Camillo Antonio -- after Rocco (13 December 1833) and Annunziata (2 December 1836). The three of them fall three years apart, twice, which is what fixes Rocco as the eldest and pushes Camillo Antonio's birth to 1841 or later. Her act has not been opened. Not in the family tree.

name: Orazio Arena (b. c. 1751)
bornNote: SEVENTY-NINE at his death on 12 July 1830 -- his own death act. This archive had inferred «about 1770» by working back from his sons and assuming a young father; he was about forty-two when Filippo was born.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1815 atto 29; Matrimoni 1821 atto 29; Matrimoni 1828 atto 26; Morti 1830 atto 64
note: THE TOP OF THE ARENA SPINE UNTIL THIS AFTERNOON, AND NOW NOT. He is a MARINARO in every record that gives him a trade, and the sea runs FIVE generations through him: his father Filippo, himself, his son Filippo, his grandson Francesco Antonio, his great-grandson Rocco. He stood at three of his sons' weddings -- Filippo's in 1815, Giuseppe's in 1821, Antonio's in 1828 -- and died at six in the morning on 12 July 1830, in his own house, with two young kinsmen to declare it. HIS OWN DEATH ACT NAMES HIS PARENTS: «figlio del fu FILIPPO ARENA e della fu SANTA UNGARO». Not in the family tree. AND THE NAMESAKE IS STILL A TRAP: the tree holds an «Orazio Arena» of generation six, father of Teresa Arena, the man it wrongly hangs Rocco Arena under. TWO DIFFERENT MEN, two generations apart.

name: Litteria Morabito
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore a parish record.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1815 atto 29; processetti 1815 n. 29, estratto di battesimo
note: FILIPPO ARENA'S MOTHER, wife of Orazio Arena (b. c. 1751). Present in person at her son's marriage on 12 November 1815 and giving her consent with her husband. THE NAME IS LITTERIA, AND THIS ARCHIVE READ IT WRONG FOR AN AFTERNOON: the civil act's hand gives something like «Setteria», but her son's BAPTISM EXTRACT, copied into the marriage bundle in Latin by the parish economo on 26 May 1815, writes «ex Horatio Arena et LITTERIA MORABITO coniugibus». Litteria is a real and common name on this coast -- from the Madonna della Lettera, patroness of Messina, across the strait -- and «Setteria» is not. The clearer document wins. Not in the family tree. SHE OUTLIVED HIM: Orazio died 12 July 1830 and she is named without «fu» in the 1838 marriage Tavola, so she was still alive on 4 September 1838, a widow of eight years.

name: Giovanni Costa
bornNote: FORTY YEARS OLD, «aetatis suae annorum quadraginta circiter», at his death on 29 March 1790 -- the parish death register's own figure, copied into his daughter's marriage bundle in 1815.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1815 atto 29; processetti 1815 n. 29, estratto di morte
note: DOMENICA COSTA'S FATHER, AND THE OLDEST DOCUMENT IN THIS ARCHIVE. His daughter's marriage bundle carries the parish death register verbatim: «Die vigesima nona mensis Martii Anno Domini millesimo septingentesimo nonagesimo, Scyllae, JOANNES DE COSTA, aetatis suae annorum quadraginta circiter, FILIUS QUONDAM JOSEPHI ET JACOBAE TURCO, legitimus vir MARTHAE ALFONZETTI» -- lying ill in bed, confessed to Rev. D. Paolo Turco, given the Viaticum and anointed, and buried in the church of S. Maria di Porto Salvo. He is written DE COSTA in Latin and COSTA in the civil act. Not in the family tree.

name: Marta Alfonzetti
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore a parish record.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1815 atto 29; processetti 1815 n. 29, estratti di battesimo e di morte
note: DOMENICA COSTA'S MOTHER, widowed in March 1790 when her husband was about forty, and still alive in November 1815, when she stood beside her daughter and consented to the marriage. She is named three times in one bundle -- in her daughter's 1787 baptism, in her husband's 1790 death, and in the 1815 civil act -- which is as firmly as anyone in this archive is attested. ALFONZETTI is a Scilla name met elsewhere in the same run: an Alfonzetti groom marries in 1817 (atto 19). Not in the family tree.

name: Giuseppe Costa
bornNote: Not sought, and probably unreachable: his son was born about 1750, so he belongs to the 1720s.
source: Scilla, processetti 1815 n. 29, estratto di morte di Giovanni Costa
note: GENERATION NINE, and reached by three documents stacked on each other: the 1815 civil marriage act named Domenica Costa's father; the marriage bundle copied his parish death act; and that act calls him «FILIUS QUONDAM JOSEPHI ET JACOBAE TURCO». QUONDAM is the whole finding -- Giuseppe was already dead when his son died in March 1790. Nothing else is known of him and nothing else is likely to be: Scilla's civil registers begin nineteen years after his son's death. Not in the family tree.

name: Giacoma Turco
bornNote: Not sought; 1720s, and pre-civil.
source: Scilla, processetti 1815 n. 29, estratto di morte di Giovanni Costa
note: GENERATION NINE. «Filius quondam Josephi et Jacobae Turco» -- the QUONDAM governs both parents, so she too was dead by March 1790. NOTE THE SURNAME: the priest who heard her son's last confession on his deathbed was REV. D. PAOLO TURCO. In a town of this size that is very likely a relative at the bedside, not a coincidence, though nothing here proves it. Not in the family tree.

name: Mariano Mazza (b. c. 1809)
bornNote: THIRTY-SIX when he declared his son Rosario's birth on 2 June 1845 -- his own statement, in person, at the comune house.
father: Ignazio Mazza (or Orazio; father of Mariano, b. c. 1809)
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1845 atto 64; Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni allegati 1871, fascicolo 14 -- «CERTIFICATO di seguita pubblicazione di matrimonio senza opposizione», 16 April 1871
note: THE TOP OF THE SICILIAN SPINE, AND HE HAS BEEN FILED ON THE WRONG MAN. His son's birth act names him in his own words; his son is entered as «Rosario Mazza DI MARIANO» in the 1873 birth of Salvatore and again in the 1871 marriage. THE NAMESAKE TRAP, AND THIS ARCHIVE WALKED INTO IT: the family tree holds a «Mariano Mazza» who is the son of the ORAZIO MAZZA BORN 1883, himself a son of Rosario -- a twentieth-century man who cannot have fathered a boy in 1845. The 1845 record was attached to that slug and sat on his person page until 20 September. He is filed here as «Mariano Mazza (b. c. 1809)» so no parent link can ever resolve to the wrong one. Not in the family tree. ALIVE ON 16 APRIL 1871, AND THE DOCUMENT SAYS SO IN A PRINTED FIELD. The publication certificate for his son Rosario's marriage reads «figlio del VIVENTE MARIANO, professione bracciante, residente anche ivi» -- not the absence of a «fu» but the positive word, written into a form that has a blank for exactly this. He was about sixty-two, still a bracciante, still living at Piedimonte Etneo.
