TWENTY-SIX YEARS AFTER his own appearance at the comune house to declare Rosario's birth, and the second document in which he speaks for himself rather than being named by a descendant. 11 NOV 2026 -- HIS PARENTS, HIS WIFE'S NAME, HIS DEATH, AND HIS OTHER CHILDREN. (1) Piedimonte Etneo Matrimoni 1836 atto 17 (8 September 1836): «Mariano Mazza, 30, son of Ignazio and Giuseppa Pulvirenti (70)» marries AGATA CATALANO, 27, daughter of the late Carlo Catalano and Maria Cardillo. (2) Piedimonte Morti 1887 atto 10: Mariano Mazza died 9 February 1887 aged EIGHTY, 'fu Orazio' and 'fu Polvirenti Giuseppa', «marito di Catalano Agata». (3) Matrimoni 1860 atti 30 and 31 name Mariano Mazza and Maria Catalano as the parents of Salvatore (b. c. 1841) and Venera (b. c. 1837), whose marriages are recorded here. INFERRED, NOT PROVED: all three are tied to THIS Mariano by his name, his age (30 in 1836, 36 in 1845, 80 in 1887 -- born 1806-09), his town, and a wife surnamed Catalano; no act says in so many words that the Mariano of 1836 or 1887 is the father of Rosario. THE FATHER'S NAME DISAGREES: Ignazio in the 1836 promise act (re-zoomed, it has an n); Orazio in the 1836 table and the 1887 death act (whose declarants were gravediggers). NOT RESOLVED. THE WIFE'S NAME DISAGREES TOO: Agata in 1836 and 1887, Maria in 1845, 1860 and 1871 -- both Catalano, so most probably the same woman known by two Christian names, but not proved. UPDATE 11 NOV 2026: HE HAS A BROTHER, GIUSEPPE MAZZA (b. c. 1811, d. 8 December 1855), son of the same Orazio Mazza and Giuseppa Pulvirenti, who married Venera Catalano (daughter of Giovanni, born at Macchia) on 31 January 1836, eight months before Mariano's own wedding (Matrimoni 1836 atto 3; Morti 1855 atto 122). The father is Orazio in both brothers' records.

name: Maria Catalano
bornNote: THIRTY-SIX at her son Rosario's birth in June 1845, the same age as her husband.
died: 18 December 1891 (Piedimonte Etneo Morti 1891 atto 118, read at the image)
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1845 atto 64; Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni allegati 1871, fascicolo 14 -- «CERTIFICATO di seguita pubblicazione di matrimonio senza opposizione», 16 April 1871; Piedimonte Etneo, Morti 1891 atto 118 (an_ua83464, image 36, read at the image)
note: ROSARIO MAZZA'S MOTHER, named in his birth act of 2 June 1845 and nowhere in the family tree. The parish of the CHIESA MAGGIORE returned the baptism notice the same day. She and Mariano were both thirty-six, so both born about 1809 -- which puts their marriage in the window the Piedimonte MATRIMONI PROCESSETTI cover from 1841, a series this archive has never opened. ALIVE ON 16 APRIL 1871: «e della VIVENTE MARIA CATALANO, professione industriosa, residente anche ivi». The same certificate that gives her husband. It is also the first record of her TRADE -- industriosa, the word these registers use for a woman doing piecework at home. 11 NOV 2026 -- HER PARENTS, INFERRED, NOT PROVED: the 1836 marriage act (Piedimonte Matrimoni 1836 atto 17) names the bride as AGATA Catalano, 27, born at Macchia, daughter of the late CARLO Catalano and of MARIA CARDILLO (60), and the 1887 death act of Mariano Mazza calls his widow «Catalano Agata»; every act that names her as Rosario's mother calls her MARIA. The 27 of 1836 agrees with the 36 of 1845 (born 1809) and not with the 59 of 1860. Same husband's name, same surname, same town: probable, but the two Christian names are unreconciled, and her parents are recorded here only on that inference. What would settle it: Rosario's baptism extract in his 1871 marriage file, or Matrimoni 1871 atto 14's own parents paragraph. 17 NOV 2026 -- HER DEATH, AND THE TWO NAMES ARE ONE WOMAN. Piedimonte Morti 1891 atto 118 (declared 19 December 1891): the margin reads «Catalano Maria Agata» and the act «AGATA CATALANO», died at seven in the evening of 18 December 1891 in via Rocca Campana, aged EIGHTY-THREE (so born about 1808, agreeing with the 27 of 1836 and the 36 of 1845), BORN AT GIARRE, daughter of the late CARLO and the late CARDILLO MARIA, and «Vedova Marza Mariano» (the surname written Marza, the husband Mariano Mazza). Declarants Salvatore Puglisi (53, contadino) and Ignazio Cali (54); witnesses Giuseppe Di Francesco (36) and Alfio Stiro (42, becchino); nobody signed, all illiterate. So Agata of the 1836 marriage and 1887 death and Maria of 1845, 1860 and 1871 are one woman, Maria Agata, and her parents Carlo Catalano and Maria Cardillo are now stated by her own death act, not inferred. Her birthplace is Giarre in the death act and Macchia in the 1836 promise (Macchia lies beside Giarre). Her widowhood was 4 years and 10 months.

name: Rosario Mazza
bornNote: Act 64 of 1845: born at eleven in the morning and declared the same day. The tree says 1850; his death act of 1924 makes him seventy-nine, which agrees with the register and not with the tree.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1845 atto 64; Matrimoni 1871 atto 14; Italy, Catania -- death 15 November 1924
note: HE IS IN THE FAMILY TREE; HIS PARENTS ARE NOT. This row exists only to carry the join: it anchors MARIANO MAZZA and MARIA CATALANO, both named in his own birth act, onto the export person the charts draw. Without it the chart closed his line with «Before Piedimonte Etneo, 1850» -- a card that reported the tree's silence and read as though the registers were silent too. They are not. He is the top of the Sicilian spine in the export; the two people above him are documented and the chart now draws them.

name: Mariano Mazza (b. 1872)
bornNote: Act 32 of 1872: born at ten in the evening of 12 February and declared at noon the next day by his father in person.
died: 8 March 1872 (Piedimonte Morti 1872 atto 22, strada Borgo, aged three weeks)
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1872 atto 32
note: SALVATORE MAZZA'S ELDER BROTHER, AND THE NAMING CUSTOM CALLED HIM. Rosario Mazza's first son is named for ROSARIO'S OWN FATHER -- exactly what the custom predicts -- which is a third independent pointer at Mariano Mazza (b. c. 1809) after the 1845 birth act and the «di Mariano» patronymic. Born in CONTRADA SAN BASILIO, the same lane the family is in when Salvatore is born eleven months later. ELEVEN MONTHS IS TIGHT: Salvatore was born 5 January 1873, so either this boy died in infancy or the two births are ten and a half months apart. Not in the family tree, and his death has not been sought. NOTE THE NAME: there are now THREE Mariano Mazza in this archive -- this baby, his grandfather (b. c. 1809), and the twentieth-century man in the family tree who is a son of the Orazio born 1883. All three are TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE twice over -- this baby of 1872, his grandfather born about 1809, and the tree's twentieth-century namesake -- and they are filed apart on purpose so that no father= in this file can resolve to the wrong one. DIED 8 MARCH 1872, three and a half weeks old (an_ua83445, image 12; read by a delegated reader): that settles the 'eleven months is tight' puzzle: the next child, Salvatore, was born 5 January 1873.

name: Gaetano Mazza
bornNote: Act 66 of 1880: born at half past four in the afternoon of 5 May and declared at a quarter past ten four days later by his father in person.
died: 10 September 1880 (Piedimonte Morti 1880 atto 122, via S. Basilio)
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1880 atto 66
note: ANOTHER SON OF ROSARIO AND LEONARDA, AND THE NAMING CUSTOM CALLED HIM TOO. «Mazza Rosario, di anni trentadue, bracciante» declared him, born to «BONANNO LEONARDA, industriosa, sua moglie» in VIA S. BASILIO -- the same lane as his brother Mariano eight years earlier, and the mother's surname is given in full, which is what tells this household apart from the other Rosario-and-Leonarda in the town. GAETANO is the name the Sicilian custom gives after the MOTHER'S FATHER, and Leonarda's father is GAETANO BONANNO, named as such in the 1872 and 1873 acts. Witnesses Dimauro Salvatore, twenty-two, and Zappala Sebastiano, twenty-four. Not in the family tree, and his death has not been sought. DIED 10 SEPTEMBER 1880, aged four months (an_ua83453, image 59; read by a delegated reader).

name: Domenico Arena (barbiere, b. c. 1743)
bornNote: SEVENTY at his son Diego's marriage on 12 August 1813, standing beside him and consenting -- so born about 1743, EARLIER THAN ANY OTHER ARENA IN THIS ARCHIVE.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1813 atto 21
note: AN ARENA HOUSEHOLD AT SCILLA WITH NO ESTABLISHED CONNECTION TO THIS FAMILY, and it is recorded here as exactly that. He is a BARBER where the spine is four generations of sailors, and the only Arena this archive has who was alive in the 1740s. His wife is ANNA MELIDONI and his eldest son DIEGO ARENA, sartore, married Maria Giuseppa Pontillo in 1813. HE IS NOT CLAIMED AS ORAZIO ARENA'S FATHER, and the temptation to claim him is the reason this note exists: Scilla has more than one Arena family, and TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE sharing a surname in one small town is how this archive nearly hung a birth act on the wrong Mariano Mazza a week ago. What would settle it is Orazio Arena's own marriage, which is pre-1809 and parish.

name: Anna Melidoni
bornNote: FIFTY-FOUR at her son Diego's marriage in August 1813.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1813 atto 21
note: Wife of Domenico Arena (barbiere, b. c. 1743), «domiciliante in casa di suo marito», present at her son's marriage and consenting with him. Like her husband she belongs to an Arena household this archive cannot yet connect to its own -- TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from the Arena of the spine until something says otherwise.

name: Diego Arena
bornNote: THIRTY-SEVEN at his marriage on 12 August 1813.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1813 atto 21
note: Married MARIA GIUSEPPA PONTILLO, sixteen, daughter of Giovanni Pontillo, forty-two, commerciante, and Diana Idone, at Scilla on 12 August 1813; the banns were published at CAMPO as well as Scilla. A TAILOR, in a family of barbers, and no established connection to the Arena of this archive's spine -- TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE until a record says otherwise. NOTE THE BRIDE'S SURNAMES: Pontillo and Idone both appear elsewhere in this archive, in the Polistena and Costa households. That is a coincidence of common Scilla names and is written down as one.

name: Carlo Arena
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore parish.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1812, Tavola annuale, atto 10
note: A THIRD ARENA FATHER AT SCILLA IN THE SAME DECADE AS ORAZIO, and no connection to him is claimed. His daughter GIOVANNA ARENA married Giovanni La Mussa on 6 January 1812; the Tavola names her parents as «Carlo, ed Eugenia Ateja». TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from the Arena of this archive's spine until a record says otherwise -- the napoleonic marriage years hold Domenico the barber, Carlo, and Orazio, three Arena fathers with nothing between them.

name: Antonia Arena
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore parish.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1811 atto 22; Matrimoni 1812 atto 1
note: DEAD BEFORE FEBRUARY 1811, and dated by two indexes rather than by an act. She is «fu Antonia Arena», wife of DOMENICO FALCOMATA, in the 1811 Tavola when her daughter GIUSEPPA FALCOMATA marries Tomaso Spoliti of Bagnara, and again in the 1812 Tavola when her daughter NUNZIATA FALCOMATA marries Angelo Porchese of Reggio. Both entries give the same parents, so the two brides are sisters and one household. No connection to this archive's Arena is claimed -- TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE until something says otherwise.

name: Giuseppe Arena (b. c. 1794)
bornNote: TWENTY-SEVEN on 7 November 1821, at his own solenne promessa -- so born about 1794.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1821 atto 29; Tavola annuale 1821
note: FILIPPO ARENA'S BROTHER, AND THE FIRST SIBLING THIS ARCHIVE HAS EVER FOUND FOR HIM. Same parents, same trade, same town: «figlio di ORAZIO ARENA, di professione MARINARO, e di LITTERIA MORABITO». He married MARIA TERESA POLISTINA at Scilla on 13 November 1821, the promessa taken six days earlier before Tommaso Cutelli, the same sindaco who married Filippo in 1815. THE AGES ARE TIGHT: Filippo was born 25 March 1793 and Giuseppe's age puts him in 1794, eight to twenty months later -- possible, and equally possible that one declared age is a year out, which is routine here. NOTE THE NAME: the family tree holds a GIUSEPPE ARENA born 1860, son of Francesco Antonio -- TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE two generations apart, and the later one is named for this one, which is what the naming custom predicts.

name: Maria Teresa Polistina
bornNote: TWENTY-ONE at her marriage on 13 November 1821, «nata in questo Comune».
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1821 atto 29; Tavola annuale 1821
note: GIUSEPPE ARENA'S WIFE, and an ARENA-POLISTINA marriage a century before the two surnames meet again in this family. Both her parents were dead by November 1821. NOTE WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this archive's Polistena line at Scilla is not connected to her, and Polistina is a common name in the town.

name: Raffaele Polistina
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore parish.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1821 atto 29
note: «RAFAELE POLISTINA, DEFONTO» at his daughter Maria Teresa's promessa on 7 November 1821, and «fu Raffaele» in the Tavola -- so dead before that date. Nothing else is known of him.

name: Vittoria Morabito
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore parish.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1821, Tavola annuale; atto 29
note: MARIA TERESA POLISTINA'S MOTHER, dead before November 1821. AND THE ARCHIVE'S TWO WITNESSES DISAGREE ABOUT HER NAME: the annual Tavola writes «Vittoria Morabito» and the act itself appears to write «Litteria Morabito, defonta» -- which is the name of the GROOM'S living mother. Two women of the name, or a clerk's eye slipping up a line. The Tavola is preferred here only because it does not repeat itself, and the doubt is recorded rather than hidden. TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from Litteria Morabito either way: one was alive that day and one was not.

name: Antonio Arena (m. 1828)
bornNote: Not sought. His brothers are 1793 and about 1794, so he is probably later in the 1790s; the marriage act itself would give his age.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 26; Tavola annuale 1828
note: FILIPPO ARENA'S SECOND BROTHER, found the same way as the first: the annual Tavola names all four parents, and this one opens on «ARENA ANTONIO e DE LUCA SERAFINA -- ORAZIO, e MORABITO LETTERIA». He married SERAFINA DE LUCA at Scilla on 10 August 1828. So Orazio Arena and Litteria Morabito had at least three sons: Filippo (b. 1793, m. 1815), Giuseppe (b. c. 1794, m. 1821) and Antonio (m. 1828). THE NAME NEEDS ITS BRACKET: this archive holds two Antonio Arena born at New York in 1896 and 1902, and the family tree holds more -- TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE, a century apart, and this row is the Scilla one.

name: Serafina de Luca
bornNote: Not sought; her marriage act would give her age.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1828, Tavola annuale, entry 1
note: ANTONIO ARENA'S WIFE, married at Scilla on 10 August 1828. Her father FILIPPO DE LUCA was already dead -- «fu Filippo» -- and her mother ANNA ALFONZETTO was living. NOTE THE SURNAME, AND NOTE THAT NOTHING IS CLAIMED FROM IT: Alfonzetto is the same name as MARTA ALFONZETTI, Domenica Costa's mother, who was alive at Scilla in 1815. Two Alfonzetti women in one family's circle is what a small town looks like, not a connection.

name: Domenico Arena (m. 1838)
bornNote: From «anni trentanove» in the birth act of his son on 5 June 1839 (Scilla, Nati 1839 atto 85). The act calls him a COMMERCIANTE.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1838 atto 20; Tavola annuale 1838; Scilla, Nati 1839 atto 85, read in the original (image 45)
note: FILIPPO ARENA'S THIRD BROTHER. The 1838 Tavola opens on him: «ARENA DOMENICO e POLISTINA TERESA -- FU ORAZIO, e Lett.a Morabito». He married TERESA POLISTINA at Scilla on 4 September 1838. HE IS ALSO THE MAN WHO DATES HIS FATHER'S DEATH: the «fu» before Orazio is the only one in any Arena entry this archive has read, and it brackets Orazio's death to the ten years after August 1828. TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from the Domenico Arena, barbiere, born about 1743 who appears in the 1813 marriage of Diego Arena -- that one is two generations up and no connection is claimed. UPDATE 17 NOVEMBER 2026: his son's birth act (Nati 1839 atto 85, read at the image) gives his age as THIRTY-NINE on 5 June 1839, so born about 1800, and his trade, commerciante; it names Teresa Polistina as his «moglie legittima», thirty-eight.

name: Teresa Polistina
bornNote: From «di anni trentotto» in her son's birth act, 5 June 1839 (Scilla, Nati 1839 atto 85).
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1838, Tavola annuale, entry 1; Scilla, Nati 1839 atto 85, read in the original (image 45)
note: DOMENICO ARENA'S WIFE, married 4 September 1838, and the SECOND Polistina daughter of «fu Raffaele e Letteria Morabito» to marry a son of Orazio Arena -- MARIA TERESA POLISTINA married his brother GIUSEPPE in 1821. EITHER TWO SISTERS MARRIED TWO BROTHERS, OR ONE WIDOW MARRIED HER BROTHER-IN-LAW. Nothing read so far settles it; the Scilla death registers of 1821-1838 would. Recorded as two people because the two Tavole give two different given names, and merging them would be a guess. UPDATE 17 NOVEMBER 2026: alive on 4 June 1839, thirty-eight, when she bore Domenico Arena's son Giuseppe, so the 1838 wife was alive and still bearing children. Her stated age (born about 1801) and Maria Teresa Polistina's (twenty-two in December 1821, so about 1799) are within the usual error of one woman, but the register gives no widowhood for Maria Teresa and the question stays open: no merge is made.

name: Santo Arena
bornNote: Not sought; pre-1809 and therefore parish.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1833, Tavola annuale; Matrimoni 1821, Tavola annuale
note: THE FATHER OF TWO ARENA GROOMS AND NOT OURS. His son ROCCO married Domenica Costa on 10 June 1821 and his son FRANCESCO married Concetta Palermo on 13 December 1833; both entries give the mother as VITTORIA FIORENZA, which is what makes them brothers. The 1833 entry writes «fu Santo», so he was dead by then; the 1821 entry's father's name is cut by the page edge and this is what supplies it. NO CONNECTION TO ORAZIO ARENA IS CLAIMED -- Scilla holds at least seven Arena households in this period.

name: Filippo Arena (the elder, d. before 1830)
bornNote: Not sought; he belongs to the 1720s and is pre-civil.
source: Scilla, Morti 1830 atto 64
note: GENERATION NINE. «FIGLIO DEL FU FILIPPO ARENA e della fu SANTA UNGARO» -- the death act of his son ORAZIO, 12 July 1830. The «fu» dates him dead before that day; his son was born about 1751, so he belongs to the 1720s and everything about him is pre-civil and parish. AND HE EXPLAINS A NAME: Orazio's first son, born 25 March 1793, is FILIPPO -- the Sicilian and Calabrian custom giving the first son his father's father. This archive used the custom to RANK candidates for four months and never once to identify one; here the act confirms it after the fact, which is the only way round that is safe. THERE ARE NOW THREE FILIPPO ARENA in this archive: this one, his grandson born 1793, and that man's grandson born 1852. All three are filed apart on purpose.

name: Santa Ungaro
bornNote: Not sought; 1720s, and pre-civil.
source: Scilla, Morti 1830 atto 64
note: ORAZIO ARENA'S MOTHER, and the second person of generation nine on this side. «Della FU Santa Ungaro» in her son's death act of July 1830, so dead before then. UNGARO is a surname new to this archive. Nothing else is known of her and nothing else is likely to be: Scilla's civil registers begin in 1809, fifty-eight years after her son was born.

name: Diego Arena (b. c. 1808)
bornNote: TWENTY-TWO when he declared his relative's death on 12 July 1830.
source: Scilla, Morti 1830 atto 64
note: ONE OF THE TWO MEN WHO DECLARED ORAZIO ARENA'S DEATH, and the act calls him «NIPOTE DEL DEFONTO» -- which in Italian is nephew OR grandson and this archive will not choose for it. A MARINARO at twenty-two, like the man he was burying. TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from the Diego Arena, sartore, who was thirty-seven in 1813: that one was born about 1776. His exact place in the household is unresolved and the Scilla birth registers of 1808 would settle it.

name: Prospero Arena
bornNote: TWENTY-FIVE when he declared Orazio Arena's death on 12 July 1830.
source: Scilla, Morti 1830 atto 64
note: THE SECOND DECLARANT AT ORAZIO ARENA'S DEATH, also «nipote del defonto» and also a MARINARO. Born about 1805, so too old to be a son of Filippo (m. 1815) or Giuseppe (m. 1821) -- which makes nephew more likely than grandson, and would mean ORAZIO HAD A BROTHER. Recorded as a question, not an answer.

name: Giuseppe Arena (d. 1925)
bornNote: Born at two in the night on 4 June 1839 (Scilla, Nati 1839 atto 85, read in the original at the image); the act was registered on 5 June.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla deaths: «Giuseppe Arena, Morte: Scilla 27/03/1925, Padre Domenico, Madre Teresa Polistena, Coniuge Serafina Vita»; Scilla, Nati 1839 atto 85, read in the original (image 45); Scilla, Matrimoni 1868 atto 2 (Giuseppe Arena of Domenico, groom, mother Teresa Polistina)
note: A CHILD OF FILIPPO ARENA'S BROTHER DOMENICO, and the first evidence that the 1838 marriage produced anyone. He died at Scilla on 27 March 1925, husband of SERAFINA VITA. THE ENTRY ALSO CONFIRMS TERESA POLISTINA INDEPENDENTLY: this archive had her only from the 1838 annual Tavola, and here she is again as a mother, eighty-seven years later, in a different series indexed by a different hand. TWO DIFFERENT PEOPLE from the Giuseppe Arena born about 1794 who is Filippo's brother, and from the Giuseppe Arena born 1860 who is Rocco's -- three men of the name in three generations of one extended family, which is what the naming custom does to an archive. UPDATE 17 NOVEMBER 2026: HE IS NOW DATED. His birth act names his father Domenico Arena, a thirty-nine-year-old commerciante, and his mother Teresa Polistina; the witnesses were Pasquale Arlotta and Giacomo Vita. He married at Scilla in 1868 (Matrimoni 1868 atto 2, read by a delegated reader from the annual index and the act, not yet by the session): Giuseppe, son of Domenico and Teresa Polistina, groom, and Serafina Vita, daughter of Giovanni. The 4 June 1839 date gives eighty-five years at death in 1925.

name: Teresa Arena (d. 1943)
bornNote: Not sought.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla deaths: «Teresa Arena, Morte: Scilla 27/08/1943, Padre Giuseppe, Madre Serafina Vita, Coniuge Gaetano Cosentino»
note: GRANDDAUGHTER OF DOMENICO ARENA AND TERESA POLISTINA, and named for her grandmother exactly as the custom predicts. She died at Scilla on 27 August 1943, wife of GAETANO COSENTINO. Her line is a cousin branch of this archive's own: her great-grandfather ORAZIO ARENA is Filippo's father. NOTHING HERE JOINS HER TO THE SPINE beyond that shared great-grandfather, and nothing should.

name: Giovanni Nicotra (John)
bornNote: FOUND 23 Nov 2026 at his own birth act: San Giovanni (a frazione of Giarre, with its own civil registers), Nati 1841 atto 3, «sette» January 1841 (Tavola «7 Genn° 1841»). Consistent with «anni trentuno» in October 1872.
source: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1872 atto 20 (7 October 1872), read in the original; San Giovanni, Nati 1841 atto 3 and its Tavola (Antenati an_ua19994298, images 5 and 64), read at the image
note: MARIA NICOTRA'S FATHER, and the man the Queensland death registration of 1963 calls «John Nicotra» and nothing else. Here he is in his own act: «sono comparsi GIOVANNI NICOTRA, di anni trentuno, di professione bracciante, DOMICILIATO E RESIDENTE A MASCALI, figlio di ROSARIO, di professione bracciante, e di VENERA MURABITO, contadina, domiciliati e residenti PURE IN MASCALI». HE IS NOT A PIEDIMONTE MAN. He married into the town and lived in the next one, which is why fourteen consecutive Piedimonte birth indexes produced no daughter of his. UPDATE 23 NOVEMBER 2026 — HIS BIRTH ACT: BORN AT SAN GIOVANNI, the Giarre of the 1872 certificate. The Nati 1841 Tavola of San Giovanni (a separate Antenati series from Giarre and Macchia, which is why eleven Giarre years and the Macchia register never held him) lists «3. Nicotra Giovanni — Rosario / Murabito Venera — 7 Genn° 1841», and act 3 (image 5) is a Nicotra child of VENERA MURABITO «di anni trenta», the baptism return reading «Giovanni Nicotra». The father's age and trade and the hour are not legible in the image; his first name rests on the Tavola. The mother's age puts her about 1811, against 32 in 1850 at Macchia: the ages of these women do not agree anywhere in this file. WHICH ROSARIO is still open: the act is of San Giovanni, so the Rosario of S. Giovanni (b. c. 1794, wife Paola Previtera) is now a live candidate beside the Simone line; the test is a San Giovanni marriage or Paola's death. SECOND UPDATE 23 NOVEMBER 2026: A SISTER IS FOUND, MARIA, born 3 April 1842 at San Giovanni (Nati 1842 atto 24), of ROSARIO NICOTRA «di anni trenta», BRACCIALE, and VENERA MORABITO. A father of thirty makes him the Milo bracciale of the Macchia acts (b. about 1812) rather than the Rosario of the Simone line or the S. Giovanni Rosario b. about 1794; the household is the one at Macchia in 1850-57. The question of which Rosario is his father is therefore narrowed, not closed: the Rosario of Mascali 1890 is called «about ninety». UPDATE 23 NOVEMBER 2026 (gap years): two further brothers found at San Giovanni, Giuseppe (b. 29 October 1845, act 92) and Sebastiano (b. 21 December 1847, act 119), and none in 1844, 1846, 1848 or 1849. The act headers read «Comune di Giarre»: San Giovanni is the register of the Giarre quartieri S. Giovanni and S. Alfio, which is why «nato a Giarre» in 1872 was right. UPDATE 23 NOVEMBER 2026: HIS PARENTS' MARRIAGE FOUND, San Giovanni Matrimoni 1839 atto 11: Rosario Nicotra (30), son of Simone and Marianna Daidone, married Venera Murabito (22), daughter of the late Salvadore, in September 1839, fifteen months before Giovanni's birth. His paternal grandparents are therefore Simone Nicotra and Marianna Daidone; the Rosario of Paola Previtera and the Rosario of Spina Rosa are not his father.

name: Venera Cassaniti
bornNote: TWENTY-FOUR on 7 October 1872, so born about 1848 -- and Piedimonte Nati 1848 atto 45 is «CASSANITI VENERA», born the fourteenth. The two fit without strain.

After three documents he has a birthplace, a birth year, a trade, a death, two parents and his wife named beside him. He was BORN AT GIARRE about 1800 — which is very likely why his son Giovanni said «nato a Giarre» — and he had moved to Mascali by 1872. Three independent acts now name him: his son's marriage in 1872, his granddaughter's birth in 1873 where he is «di Rosario» and alive, and his own death. UPDATE 23 NOVEMBER 2026: THE MARRIAGE ACT NAMES HIM AND CONFIRMS THE LINK: San Giovanni Matrimoni 1839 atto 11 gives Rosario Nicotra, thirty, a bracciale born at San Giovanni, son of Simone and Marianna Daidone, marrying Venera Murabito, twenty-two, daughter of the late Salvadore. The 1890 act («da fu Simone … marito di Murabito Venera») is this man, who is also the Milo bracciale of the Macchia acts (see that row). Two figures in the 1890 act do not fit and are left as written: «novanta circa» (the marriage act points to a birth about 1809) and the mother «Musumeci» (the marriage act says Daidone). The two rows are not merged here; the identity rests on the father Simone and the wife Venera Murabito agreeing in two independent acts.

GIOVANNI (BATTISTA), a contadino, with a wife Paola Previtera of the same age bracket (28) and two daughters registered a year apart. HE IS A CANDIDATE FOR THE ROSARIO OF THE SIMONE LINE AND NOTHING MORE: his acts name no parents, and the arithmetic is against it — born about 1794 he would be six years older than the Rosario of 1890 («novanta circa»), and Marianna Daidone, Simone's wife, was «quaranta» in April 1820 and would have been fourteen at his birth. The 1872 certificate gives Giovanni Nicotra's mother as VENERA MURABITO, not Paola Previtera, so if he is the same man Paola would have to have died and Venera been a second wife. NOT LINKED; no marriage, death or later child has been found for him.

name: Rosario Nicotra (the Milo bracciale, husband of Venera Morabito)
bornNote: «Quaron...to» in the 1850 act (probably forty-eight, giving about 1802), «quarantacinque» in 1857 (about 1812) and about forty-two in 1855: the three ages do not agree.
source: Macchia, Nati 1850 atto 159, 1855 atto 6 and 1857 atto 202, read in the original; Nati 1852 atto 48 (Tavola)
note: A bracciale domiciled at MILO, who declared four children's births between 1850 and 1857. THE STRONG CANDIDATE FOR THE ROSARIO NICOTRA OF THE SIMONE LINE: the 1872 marriage papers of Giovanni Nicotra name his parents ROSARIO NICOTRA and VENERA MURABITO (a bracciante, living at Mascali), and this man's wife is VENERA MORABITO, 32 in 1850, 36 in 1855 and 40 in 1857; a Giovanni born about 1841 fits her age. AGAINST: the Rosario of the 1890 death act was «about ninety» (born about 1800), and his ages here run 42-48; and no Giovanni is in the Macchia birth registers of 1841 or 1847 (the 1872 certificate says Giarre). NOT CLAIMED AS THE SAME MAN; the test is the Giarre or Mascali record that links the two, and Rosario's own parents, which none of these acts names. MACCHIA, a comune beside Giarre later absorbed into it; filed under Giarre because Macchia and Milo are not on the map.  UPDATE 23 NOVEMBER 2026: THE «NO GIOVANNI IN 1841» ABOVE IS WITHDRAWN. Giovanni was born on 7 January 1841 at SAN GIOVANNI (Nati 1841 atto 3, Venera Murabito aged thirty), a separate comune from Macchia, so the Macchia silence never applied. The San Giovanni act does not say Milo. UPDATE 23 NOVEMBER 2026 (second): SAN GIOVANNI Nati 1842 atto 24 names «ROSARIO NICOTRA, di anni TRENTA, bracciale, domiciliato in S. Giovanni» and «VENERA MORABITO» as the parents of Maria (b. 3 April 1842). A bracciale of about thirty in 1842 is the Milo bracciale (his Macchia ages are 42-48 in 1850-57), so the Giovanni of 1841 and the Milo family are now very probably ONE household: Giovanni 1841, Maria 1842, Giovanna 1850, Francesco 1852, Salvadore 1855, Angela 1857. Still not tied to a named father: no act gives his parents, and the Rosario who died at Mascali in 1890 «about ninety» is 12 or more years older than this man. UPDATE 23 NOVEMBER 2026 (gap years): San Giovanni Nati 1845 act 92 gives him «di anni trentasei [as read]» and 1847 act 119 «di anni trentadue [as read]»: the ages disagree with each other (and with «trenta» in 1842), so they fix a birth between about 1809 and 1815 and no closer; none of the three is a figure to build a year on. The Rosario of S. Alfio (wife Spina Rosa) has his own children in the same Tavolas (Gaetano 1842, Giuseppe 1844, Maria 1846, Maria 1848) and is not this man. MARRIAGE FOUND, 23 NOVEMBER 2026, AND IT SETTLES WHOSE SON HE IS: San Giovanni Matrimoni 1839 atto 11 (promise of 18 September, celebration in the same month, the Parroco's certificate of 4 October 1839): «ROSARIO NICOTRA, di anni TRENTA, nato in S. Giovanni, di professione BRACCIALE, domiciliato in S. Alfio [as read], FIGLIO DI SIMONE, di anni settanta [as read], bracciale, domiciliato in S. Giovanni, e di MARIANNA DAIDONE, di anni settanta [as read]», marrying «VENERA MURABITO, di anni VENTIDUE, nata in S. Giovanni, figlia del fu SALVADORE e di [Sebastiana] SPINA [as read]». He is therefore the Rosario of the Simone line, and the Rosario who died at Mascali in 1890 as «da fu Simone, marito di Murabito Venera»: the two rows describe ONE MAN. His birth is about 1809 (thirty in 1839), at San Giovanni, not about 1800 at Giarre: the 1890 act's «novanta circa» is ten years too many and its mother «Musumeci» disagrees with the Daidone of the marriage act (not settled which clerk slipped). The Rosario of Paola Previtera (b. about 1794) is a different man.

MARRIED 1839: San Giovanni Matrimoni 1839 atto 11 names her «Venera Murabito», 22, born at San Giovanni, daughter of the late Salvadore and of [Sebastiana] Spina, bride of Rosario Nicotra, son of Simone (see her Mascali row and the Rosario row).

Alfio of the Comune di Giarre: «Alfio Murabito», born and domiciled at San Giovanni, bracciale, son of the late Salvadore and of the late Sebastiana Spina, died in his own house (the declarants are a bottegaio of San Giovanni, Filippo [surname not settled], aged forty, and a carpenter, aged fifty; neither is a Nicotra or a Murabito). Venera Murabito married Rosario Nicotra at San Giovanni in September 1839 as the daughter of the late Salvadore and a Spina (San Giovanni Matrimoni 1839 atto 11), so Alfio is very probably her brother: the same father's name, the same mother's surname, the same quarter, the same trade. The act does not say so and no sibling is named in it, so this is PROBABLE, NOT PROVED. Nothing else is known of him.

UPDATE 23 NOVEMBER 2026: A DAIDONE WOMAN OF THE SAME QUARTER, NOT SHOWN TO BE KIN. San Giovanni Morti 1841 atto 3 (Antenati an_ua19994257, image 4, right page), 16 January 1841: «Angela Daidone», aged sixty-three (as read), born and domiciled at S. Alfio, contadina, daughter of the late Giuseppe [Daidone] and the late Venera Patane, died in her own house. The surname, the quarter and the generation (born about 1778; Marianna about 1780) fit a sister, but the act names no sibling and no Nicotra, so it is a lead and nothing more. Marianna's own death was not found in the San Giovanni Tavole of 1840-1846 (see data/nicotra-sweeps.tsv). UPDATE 24 NOVEMBER 2026: A CANDIDATE DEATH, NOT A FINDING. San Giovanni Morti 1860 atto 25 (Antenati an_ua19994275, image 15, right page), 9 October 1860: «Marianna Musumeci», aged ninety (as read), campagnola, born at San Giovanni, daughter of the late Antonino and of the late Olivera [as read] Nicotra. She bears the surname Rosario's 1890 death act gives his mother, and ninety fits the «settanta» of 1839; but the act names no husband, so it does not say she was the wife of Simone Nicotra. The Tavole of 1840-1855 hold no Marianna Daidone or Musumeci, and the acts of 1856-1862 hold no Daidone.

note: HIS DEATH IS FOUND, AS AN EXTRACT, AND HIS NAME IS ORAZIO. The marriage files of his daughters Domenica (1842) and Alfia (1844) both contain the certified extract of Piedimonte Morti 1828 act 66, listed as 'atto di morte di Orazio Mazza padre della sposa': Orazio Mazza, eighty, bracciale, born at Mascali, died 8 September 1828 at 2 a.m. in the countryside of Piedimonte, son of the late Innocenzio and the late Antonia Sapienza; the extract names no wife. Both daughters' baptisms (19 December 1815 and 15 December 1812) name «Horatius Mazza» and Josepha Pulvirenti, so Orazio, not Ignazio, is the father's name in the church books; the 1836 promise's 'Ignazio' is therefore the misreading or the slip. CAUTION: at eighty he is some thirty to forty years older than Giuseppa Pulvirenti and fathered Alfia at about sixty-four; the age may be exaggerated, or a first marriage may lie behind them. THE ACT IS NOW OPENED (12 Nov 2026, an_ua72293 image 36 left page, re-zoomed at 1600 px): act 66, 8 September 1828, 'Orazio Mazza di anni ottanta' (the surname's double z is cursive; it reads Mazza), 'nato in questo territorio' (born in THIS TERRITORY, which means Piedimonte's, NOT written Mascali: the 'Mascali' of the closing table and of the extract's earlier reading is the readers' gloss on 'Idem' and is not borne out by the act), son of the late (fu) Innocenzio and of the late Antonia Sapienza; died at 2 in the afternoon (not 2 in the morning) in the countryside of this territory; the declarants are Alessandro Buccio (50, bracciale, strada Difesa) and Gaetano Cassaniti (40, vettaniere), who cannot write; the sindaco Domenico Vacy? signs; no wife is named. His birth has not been opened: if Mascali, the Bourbon registers there begin in 1820 and he is earlier, so the baptism is a parish record. THE 1828 REGISTER'S CLOSING TABLE (Morti 1828 row 66, an_ua72293 image 53, re-zoomed) lists «Mazza [?]razio, Idem (Mascali), Mazza Innocenzio, 8 September» with the first letter under an ink blot; an earlier reading of the blot as Ignazio is not borne out by the zoom, which shows the letters -razio, and the extract spells it Orazio. HIS CHILDREN, AS NOW READ: Mariano (b. c. 1809), Giuseppe (c. 1811), Alfia (1812), Domenica (1815), Innocenzio (d. 1876, aged 'eighty') and Rosa (c. 1819), by Giuseppa Pulvirenti; Innocenzio's mother is written ANGELA Pulvirenti.

note: MARIANO, GIUSEPPE, DOMENICA AND ALFIA MAZZA'S MOTHER, AND HER DEATH IS FOUND. Morti 1843 atto 60 (an_ua72308, image 33, left page; the act's text was re-zoomed by the session): on 25 December 1843 at eight in the morning died at Piedimonte «Giuseppa Pulvirenti, di anni se[ssan]ta, moglie di fu Orazio Mazza, nata in Piedimonte, filandiera, figlia di fu Mariano e di fu Agata Barbagallo»; declarants Mastro Orazio Cardile (muratore) and Francesco Morabito (bracciale). WHAT IT SETTLES: (1) she is the mother of the four known children (Mariano, Giuseppe, Domenica, Alfia), who name her in their notices and acts; (2) her father was MARIANO PULVIRENTI and her mother AGATA BARBAGALLO, both dead by 1843, so Mariano Mazza (b. c. 1809) carries his maternal grandfather's name, as the naming custom says (and his own son Rosario's first son, Mariano, b. 1872, carries it again); (3) her husband ORAZIO MAZZA was dead before December 1841 and, if the 1836 acts say 'fu' for him, before January 1836: his own death has not been looked for (Morti tables before 1836 were read for Mazza and Marza only from 1834). Her age at death makes Mariano's birth year (c. 1809) arithmetic possible for her at any of the ages quoted.

HER DEATH IS FOUND, 15 NOV 2026, IN A REGISTER WITH NO INDEX: Piedimonte Etneo, Morti 1881 atto 85 (an_ua83454, image 40, re-zoomed by the session), the margin reading «Mazza Venera» and the act «MASSA VENERA»: «quarantacinque, contadina, nata in Piedimonte Etneo, da MARIANO, bracciante, e da CATALANO MARIA, industriosa, MOGLIE DI PATANE GIOVANNI». Her age agrees with the baptism of 1837 within a year, and the act names the same parents as her baptism certificate and her marriage: MARIANO MAZZA AND MARIA CATALANO, who carry no «fu» and so were alive on 19 August 1881 (Mariano died 9 February 1887, his wife is «Catalano Agata» in that act: the wife of this Mariano is called Maria here as in 1845, 1860 and 1871). Declarants Salvatore Guarnera and Carmelo Currenti, witnesses the two gravediggers. She was BORN AT PIEDIMONTE according to this act, not at Linguaglossa as her baptism certificate says: the two disagree, and the certificate of 1837, a parish document, is the better witness of the birth. SHE WAS NEVER IN ANY INDEX because the 1881 volume has no annual index and the earlier sweep of that year read the margins for Patane and Suderi only; she was found by a margin walk of acts 69-173 for her own name. Her baby daughter Orazia had died on 31 July 1881, nineteen days before her.

note: Husband of Venera Mazza and brother of Leonarda Patane (wife of Salvatore Mazza). Born at GIARRE, so the Patane family came to Piedimonte from there. CHECK OPEN (12 Nov 2026): the Giarre Nati 1822 table (an_ua68980) carries no Patani Giovanni, and its act 50 is a Grasso girl declared 17 July 1822, so the extract's year or number needs re-reading before this birth is tied to a register line. CHECKED AT THE IMAGES 12 NOV 2026 (session): in the Giarre Nati 1822 register itself (an_ua68980) one act runs to an image (act 1 is image 3, 2 January; act 10 image 12; act 14 image 16; act 28 image 30), so act 47 (image 50, 8 June), act 48 (image 51, 25 June, a girl of Antonino Papisarda? and Maria Barbagallo) and act 50 (image 53, a Grasso girl born 6 June) are the whole of June to early July: no act of 22 June, and none for Alfio Patane. The extract itself (an_ua72236 image 211) reads Num. d'ordine 'cinquantesimo', the year 'milleottocento ventidue', 22 June, 1 pm, and names an officer (Don Michele ...) who is not the acting mayor of the register (Don Paolo Mugumeci, second elect), so it was drawn from another series or copy, not from this one; the Giarre 1822 'Diversi' volume (an_ua68778, container not yet looked up) is the next place to look; the 1821 marriage of his parents settles the family regardless. READ 11 NOV 2026: the Giarre extract spells the mother SUDERI (not Sudero); it fixes his parents and the family at San Giovanni di Giarre in 1822. FOUND 13 NOV 2026, AND THE PUZZLE IS ANSWERED: the act is not in Giarre's own Nati 1822 because S. GIOVANNI KEPT ITS OWN REGISTERS, which Antenati lists under a separate comune 'San Giovanni' (Stato civile della restaurazione, Catania, 155 registers, 1822-1865). The act is there, atto 50 of 1822, with the officer the extract names - the archdeacon and parish priest of S. Giovanni and S. Alfio, acting as civil officer - which is exactly why the officer did not match Giarre's mayor. Witnesses Lorenzo Sanzeri (28) and Giuseppe Patane (about 28), the latter almost certainly the Giuseppe Patane (25, of S. Giovanni Battista) who witnessed his parents' marriage the year before. The register's annual tavola names the child and both parents, and spells the mother SUDERO where the act writes SUDERI. 13 NOV 2026 (later), WHAT THE SERIES IS - and this archive has now had to soften the claim twice, so it is put here at the strength the acts support and no higher. Antenati catalogues «San Giovanni» as a series in its own right (fondo 63946, serie 73630), beside Giarre (68775) and Macchia (69905); in the Catania archive the year 1830 alone has 51 such series, several of them places that are frazioni today. The officer of these acts is the ELETTO PARTICOLARE of the quarters of S. Giovanni e S. Alfio - an archdeacon in the 1820s, and by 1834 a GIUSEPPE PATANÈ who signs «L'Eletto Particolare». AND THE COMUNE NAMED IN THE ACTS CHANGES: 1822 and 1825 say «del Comune di GIARRE», 1828, 1830 and 1834 say «del Comune di DETTI QUARTIERI». So the quarters kept their own register under their own officer, and between 1825 and 1828 the clerk stopped naming Giarre; whether they were ever a comune in their own right is NOT established and is claimed neither way. What is settled, and is why this birth looked unregistered for two days, is that an act of these quarters is in this series and NOT in Giarre's own volumes. Anyone working the Giarre-Mascali-Riposto corner of Catania should enumerate the archive's series for the year before writing a nil on a comune. HIS DEATH IS FOUND, 14 Nov 2026, AND IT CONFIRMS THIS MORNING'S WORK FROM THE OTHER END OF HIS LIFE. «è morto PATANÈ GIOVANNI di anni sessanta, bracciante, residente in questo Comune, NATO IN S. GIOVANNI, da FU ALFIO, e da FU SUDERI MARIA, VEDOVO DI MAZZA VENERA». The archive believed until today that he was «born at Giarre» and that his birth act was missing; his own death act, sixty-three years later, says he was born at S. GIOVANNI - the quarter whose separate register gave up his birth act this morning. The act had been sitting in a Piedimonte volume this archive had already swept, but swept for Mazza only. Sixty is two years out from his birth of 22 June 1822, which is ordinary in a death act. Both parents are «fu», so Alfio Patane and Maria Suderi were both dead by 5 April 1885. His brother Rosario, fifty, was a declarant on the next act of the same page.

note: MARIANO MAZZA'S BROTHER, PROVED BY HIS DEATH ACT. Morti 1855 atto 122 (an_ua72323, image 64, left page; the act's own text, re-zoomed by the session): on 8 December 1855 at nine in the morning died at Piedimonte «Giuseppe Mazza, di anni quarantaquattro, marito di Venera Catalano», born at Piedimonte, bracciale, «figlio di fu Orazio [the first letter is a flourished O, read Grazio by the delegate] e di fu Giuseppa Pulvirenti». The declarants were Salvatore Barbagallo (44, bracciale) and Giuseppe Pagano (34, bracciale), both of Piedimonte. WHAT THIS SETTLES: (1) the father's name is ORAZIO, as the 1836 table and the 1887 death act of Mariano say, and not Ignazio (the word in the 1836 promise act); (2) Giuseppa Pulvirenti, Mariano's mother, is also the mother of this Giuseppe, so the two households (Mariano and Maria Catalano; Giuseppe and Venera Catalano) are those of two brothers; (3) the 'third household' recorded from the 1836-37 birth tables is NOT unconnected: it is Mariano's brother's. His own marriage is Matrimoni 1836 atto 3 (promise 30 January, wedding 31 January 1836; he was 25; Venera Catalano was born at Macchia and lived at San Basilio; her parents Giovanni and Giuseppa are not those of Mariano's wife, Carlo Catalano and Maria Cardillo, so the two Catalano wives are not sisters). Children known: Santo (b. 1 November 1836, died 6 November 1836), Giuseppa (b. 11 October 1837) and a Giuseppe who died as a child on 27 August 1839 (Morti 1839 row 66); no birth for him is found.

'Domenica, daughter of Orazio, 27, living at Piedimonte, daughter of the late Orazio and of Giuseppa Pulvirenti, 60' marries PIETRO SORBELLO (31, bracciale, son of Gioachino and Serafina Lo Coco): the form was affixed on Sunday 26 December 1841 and the wedding is Matrimoni 1842 atto 5 (promise dated 15 January 1842). She has the same parents as Mariano and Giuseppe. Her children, death and burial are not sought; the Sorbello household needs the Nati tables read for Sorbello, which was not part of this sweep. THE MARRIAGE FILE IS READ: the promise is dated 22 January 1842 and the couple were married that day; the file holds the baptisms of both and the death extract of her father Orazio (Morti 1828 act 66). Her birth date is exact. HER DEATH IS FOUND, WITH TWO DOUBTS: Morti 1872 atto 61 (an_ua83445, image 27; read by a delegated reader): 'Domenica, wife of Pietro Sorbello', daughter of the late Orazio, died 30 July 1872 at five in the afternoon, strada Borgo; the age is given as FIFTY against fifty-six by the baptism of 1815, and the mother is read 'Giuseppa Palizzenti?/Palizzotti?', not Pulvirenti. The husband and the father agree; the doubt is the age and the mother's surname. One declarant is Pasquale Mazza 'di Lenzio', relationship not stated.

name: Rosario Patane (b. 1828, of Alfio and Maria Suderi)
bornNote: San Giovanni (a quarter of Giarre with its own civil register), Nati 1828 atto 68, read 13 Nov 2026 at an_ua19994285 image 71 and re-zoomed by the session: declared on the day of birth by his father.
died: 7 August 1886, in a house «case sparse», Piedimonte Etneo (Morti 1886 atto 75: dated the 8th, the death at 11.30 p.m. «di jeri»)
source: San Giovanni, Nati 1828 atto 68 (an_ua19994285, image 71), with the annual tavola at image 110 («Patane Rosario, d'Alfio e di Maria Sudero»); read by a delegated reader and re-zoomed by the session; Piedimonte Etneo, Morti 1886 atto 75 (an_ua83459, image 38), found in the annual index by a delegated reader and opened and re-zoomed by the session; Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1858 atto 11 (an_ua72278, images 23-24), the solemne promessa of 6 April 1858, church celebration 8 May; found in the year's closing table by a delegated reader and re-zoomed by the session; Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni processetti 1858, foglio 11 (an_ua72234, images 76-82), the bundle of documents behind the marriage; found by bisection by a delegated reader and the key page re-zoomed by the session
note: A CHILD OF ALFIO PATANE AND MARIA SUDERI THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT KNOW. Born 23 August 1828 and declared the same day at sixteen o'clock by his father Alfio Patane, 30, contadino, living in the quarter of S. Giovanni; the mother is written «Maria Sudero». Baptised the same day by the parish priest of Giarre and S. Giovanni; the document is at folio 121. The witnesses are faint and not settled (a Salvadore Andriano?, 43 or 44, calzolaio, and a Mastro Salvadore whose surname is unread). He is named for his paternal grandfather Rosario Patane. Nothing is known of him after this act: he is not the Rosario Patane who appears at Piedimonte in 1860 as the son of a Giuseppe, and no death has been sought. HIS WHOLE LIFE AFTER THE BIRTH ACT ARRIVED IN ONE DOCUMENT, 14 Nov 2026 - and he was unknown to this archive until this morning. «è morto PATANÈ ROSARIO di anni sessanta, bracciante, residente in questo Comune, NATO IN GIARRE, da FU ALFIO, e da FU SUDERI MARIA, MARITO DI SCIACCA MARIA». So he left S. Giovanni with the family, lived to about fifty-eight, worked as a labourer at Piedimonte Etneo and married a MARIA SCIACCA. «Sessanta» is three years out from his birth of 23 August 1828. His brother Giovanni had died sixteen months before him, and Rosario was a declarant at that death. HIS MARRIAGE IS FOUND, 14 Nov 2026, and it fills the gap between the birth act found this morning and the death act found this afternoon. Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1858 atto 11: «ROSARIO PATANÈ di anni TRENTA, bracciale, domiciliato in Piedimonte, FIGLIO DI ALFIO, bracciale, domiciliato in Piedimonte, E DI MARIA SUDERO, domiciliata ivi», marrying MARIA SCIACCA, 24, born at Piedimonte. The promise was made 6 April 1858 and the church celebration followed on 8 May. THE SESSION RE-ZOOMED THE BRIDE'S NAME because the reader had it as ANTONIA Sciacca, which would have implied a second marriage: the act reads MARIA Sciacca, and his death act of 1886 calls him «marito di Sciacca Maria». ONE WIFE, not two. NEITHER PARENT CARRIES «fu» AND BOTH ARE DOMICILED AT PIEDIMONTE, so Alfio Patane and Maria Suderi were alive and living there in April 1858. Thirty in 1858 means born about 1828, which matches his birth act of 23 August 1828 exactly. The act cites «volume de' documenti al FOGLIO 11», which is the pointer into the Piedimonte marriage processetti of 1858 - a bundle this archive has never opened. THE 1858 MARRIAGE BUNDLE WAS OPENED 15 NOV 2026 AND IT CONTAINS A CERTIFIED COPY OF HIS BIRTH ACT, WHICH IS AN INDEPENDENT CHECK ON YESTERDAY'S FIND AND IT PASSES IN EVERY FIELD. The extract gives «Num. d'ordine SESSANTOTTO» - the session re-zoomed that word itself, because a delegated reader had read it as seventy-eight - with the birth of 23 August 1828, the baptism at S. GIOVANNI, the document at FOLIO 121, and the parents ALFIO PATANE, 30, and MARIA SUDERO, 30. Every one of those matches the act found in the San Giovanni register on 14 November: same act number, same date, same folio, same parents, same ages. So an office at Piedimonte in 1858, asked to prove where this man was born, went to the SAN GIOVANNI quarter register and copied act 68 out of it. That is official confirmation, from the period itself, that the quarter series is where this family's births belong - the point this archive spent two days establishing. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN READING OF THE MARRIAGE ACT, both from the reader and both accepted: the promise is dated SEDICI (16) APRIL 1858, not the 6th as the session first read it; and MARIA SCIACCA is TWENTY-SEVEN, not twenty-four. Her own birth extract in the same bundle gives 8 November 1831, which makes her twenty-six turning twenty-seven in April 1858 - so twenty-seven is right and the session's «ventiquattro» was wrong.

name: Angela Patane (b. 1830, of Alfio and Maria Suderi)
bornNote: San Giovanni (a quarter of Giarre with its own civil register), Nati 1830 atto 42, read 13 Nov 2026 at an_ua19994287 image 45 and re-zoomed by the session. The day may be 27 or 28: the act's «ventisette» is clear but the declaration and the birth are on the same day and the wording was not fully settled.
died: 3 February 1889, at Via Etnea, Piedimonte Etneo (Morti 1889 atto 14: dated the 4th, the death at one o'clock «di ieri»), aged fifty-eight
source: San Giovanni, Nati 1830 atto 42 (an_ua19994287, image 45); the year has NO annual tavola, so the register's 117 acts were walked one by one by a delegated reader and the act re-zoomed by the session; Piedimonte Etneo, Morti 1889 atto 14 (an_ua83462, image 7, left-hand lower act), found in the annual index by a delegated reader and opened and re-zoomed by the session
note: A CHILD OF ALFIO PATANE AND MARIA SUDERI THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT KNOW, and the only one that no index would ever have given up: 1830 is the single year of the San Giovanni birth run with no annual table, and she was found by reading all 117 acts. A girl, presented at fifteen o'clock by her father Alfio Patane, 29, bracciale, of the quarter; the mother is written «Maria Sudero», 28; the baptism column names her «Angela Patane» and dates the baptism the same day. Witnesses read at medium zoom only and not settled: a Giuseppe Patane?, 30?, and Mastro Angelo Cavallaro, 24, both marinaio. Nothing is known of her after this act; no death has been sought. She is the fourth child of the couple found at San Giovanni, after Giovanni (1822), Venera (1825) and Rosario (1828). HER DEATH IS FOUND, 14 Nov 2026, AND THE AGE FITS EXACTLY. «è morta PATANÈ ANGELA di anni CINQUANTOTTO, industriosa, residente in questo Comune, NATA IN GIARRE, da FU ALFIO, e da FU SCUDERI MARIA, MOGLIE DI TROVATO ANGELO». Fifty-eight in February 1889 means born in 1830 - and her birth act, found this morning in a year that has no index and had to be walked act by act, is 27 April 1830. The two agree to the year, which is rare in these registers and is the strongest corroboration this archive has for any of today's finds. She married ANGELO TROVATO and lived at Piedimonte Etneo. NOTE THE MOTHER'S SURNAME: this act writes SCUDERI where her brothers' acts of 1885 and 1886 write SUDERI. Same woman, same husband, three children; the clerk's hand differs. Scuderi is also a real and separate surname in these same registers, so it has gone into the Atlas catalogue as a case-by-case form, to be judged act by act and never assumed. HER MARRIAGE IS FOUND, 15 NOV 2026: Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1854 atto 20 (an_ua72274, images 41-43, re-zoomed by the session), the promise of 23 November 1854 at one in the night, the church celebration on 27 November, to ANGELO TROVATO, 24, bracciale, born and living at Piedimonte, son of fu FRANCESCO and of GIUSEPPA TROVATO, 60, living. She is «ANGELA PATANE, 24, nata in Giarre, figlia di ALFIO, 53, bracciale, e di MARIA SUDERO, 53», both living and both at Piedimonte: so Alfio Patane and Maria Suderi were alive in November 1854. The act lists three documents: the groom's birth act, the bride's birth act, and the DEATH ACT OF FRANCESCO TROVATO, the groom's father; it cites the volume of documents at FOGLIO 20, the pointer into the Piedimonte marriage processetti of 1854 (an_ua72230), not yet opened. THE WIDOWER IS NOW ALMOST CERTAIN: the 1890 groom of Matrimoni 1890 atto 28 (an_ua83411, image 31) is ANGELO TROVATO, sixty, son of fu Francesco and fu GIUSEPPA TROVATO, born at Piedimonte, a macellaio: the same father, the same mother's name and the same age (24 in 1854, 60 in 1890), nineteen months after her death. The 1890 act does not say «vedovo», so it is graded a very strong inference and not a document. A NAMESAKE TO KEEP APART: the Angela Patane who married Salvatore Barbagallo in 1850 (Matrimoni 1850 atto 8) is the daughter of fu Giuseppe and Agata Nicifora, not of Alfio, and is the widow of Barbagallo whose death is Piedimonte Morti 1878 atto 30.

note: THE OLDEST DOCUMENTED PERSON THIS ARCHIVE HAS REACHED IN THIS CORNER OF SICILY, AND THE PROOF THAT THE METHOD WORKS. He died on 20 January 1809 - ELEVEN YEARS BEFORE SICILY HAD ANY CIVIL REGISTRATION AT ALL - and he is here because the parish priest wrote out a Latin extract from the burial book in March 1858 so that his grandson's marriage could go ahead, and the civil office filed it. That is exactly the route past 1820 this archive has been looking for: a PARISH document copied into a CIVIL bundle. It did not work for the Patane or the Suderi, whose grandparents were still alive when their children married and so needed no such proof; it worked for the Sciacca because Santo was dead and Paolo before him. The lesson for the next session is that a processetto is worth opening in proportion to how many of the spouses' parents and grandparents were DEAD at the marriage.

Her birth would be in the San Giovanni register of 1824 (about); it has not been looked for. A SORBELLO LINK: her second-generation descendants may include the Sorbello who married Patane women in 1883 and 1886; no link is claimed. 15 NOV 2026, HER BAPTISM FOUND IN THE 1852 BUNDLE, and it is a PARISH document, not a civil one: «Anno Domini millesimo octingentesimo vigesimo quarto, die sexto Januarii 1824. Ego Sac. D. Joseph Spina, Coadjutor Ecclesiae S. Joannis Baptistae ... et quarterii S. Joannis, baptizavi infantem hodie natam ex ALPHIO PATANE et MARIA SUDIERE jugalibus, cui impositum fuit nomen MARIA. Matrina fuit Josepha ... uxor Angeli? Patane», certified at Giarre in July 1852 by the archpriest Don Salvator Fiamingo (surname read) and vidimated on 11 October 1852 by the Eletto Particolare. THE GODMOTHER'S SURNAME AND THE WORD BEFORE «Patane» ARE NOT SETTLED. WHY THE SAN GIOVANNI CIVIL REGISTER DID NOT GIVE HER UP: the annual tavola of San Giovanni Nati 1824 was read in full for this couple and was nil, so the civil act of a child baptised on 6 January 1824 is either absent from that year or filed under another name; the parish book is the only witness found. The foglio of the bundle is NOT 32 as the 1852 promise was read: it is the fascicolo of promessa 37 (images 217-224), the marginal label reading «Salvatore Sorbello, Maria Patane». Her husband's side is documented in the same bundle, see Salvatore Sorbello.

Angela died on 3 February 1889; on 11 September 1890 an Angelo Trovato of the same age and the same parents married CATERINA DELPOPOLO, 24, born at Linguaglossa, daughter of Francesco and Carmela Petrocitto (spelling read), both living at Linguaglossa. The 1890 act does not say widower; the identity of the two men is a very strong inference from father, mother and age. 15 NOV 2026, THE 1854 BUNDLE OPENED (foglio 20 = promessa 20, images 128-132): it holds three documents and no more, his civil birth extract (Piedimonte Nati 1830 atto 23, 11 February 1830, presented by Francesco Trovato, 32, macellajo, and Giuseppa Trovato, 36), Angela's civil birth extract (Sei Quartieri / San Giovanni, Nati 1830 atto 42, 26 April 1830) and the DEATH ACT OF FRANCESCO TROVATO (Piedimonte Morti 1850 atto 86). So his birth date is now known, and the Angelo of 1890, said to be sixty, was in fact sixty in 1890 to the year. A witness to his 1830 birth is written Lorenzo Suderi? or Sudiero?, a bracciante: a Suderi at Piedimonte in 1830, whom no one has tied to Maria Suderi's family.

note: A PRE-CIVIL DEATH, the oldest dated one in this archive on any Patane side: «Anno Domini millesimo octingentesimo tertio, die decimo sexto Martii 1803. Sebastianus Sorbello sponsus Stallae? et supra annos 65 vixit domi in C.S.M.E. (in communione Sanctae Matris Ecclesiae), animam Deo reddidit, munitus debitis Sacramentis, cujus corpus associatum fuit per me Sacerdotem D. Philippum Vaccitti? ... et in eadem sepultus est die quo supra», certified at Giarre on 22 (month illegible) 1852 by the archpriest and vidimated in October. THE WIFE'S NAME IS READ «Stallae» or «Stellae?» AND IS NOT SETTLED. It is a proof that the Giarre parish books of the late eighteenth century survive and can be certified: the extract was made to prove a death for a marriage, which is the route by which a pre-1820 act reached a civil file.

name: Giacomo Comerci (second husband of Caterina Cichello)
bornNote: SEVENTY at his death on 24 May 1848 («di anni settanta»), which gives about 1778; at his marriage on 1 October 1838 he was given as FIFTY-THREE («di anni cinquantatré»), about 1785. The two declared ages disagree by seven years; both are the clerks' statements, and the later one is used here because it is the death act, whose declarants (Vincenzo Artesi, 40, and Antonio Mannella, 36) were not his family. Born at Briatico.
trade: bracciale (day labourer) at his death; magnaio (miller) at his marriage
source: Briatico, Morti 1848, atto 6 (an_ua87706, image 5, left page, read at the image by the session); Briatico, Matrimoni 1838, atto 2 (an_ua87652, image 3); Briatico, Morti 1817, atto 39 (an_ua87675, image 21); Briatico, Morti 1818, atto 10 (an_ua87676, image 7); Briatico, Morti 1819, atti 10 and 11 (an_ua87677, image 7); Briatico, Morti 1827, atto 21 (an_ua87685, image 13)
note: Caterina Cichello's SECOND HUSBAND, married at Briatico on 1 October 1838, and DEAD BY 24 MAY 1848: his death act (atto 6, noon, in his own house, declared by Vincenzo Artesi and Antonio Mannella) calls him «marito di Catarina Cichello», with no «fu», so she was alive on that day, and names his parents as Francesco Comerci, bracciale, «defunto», and Catarina Mannella, «defunta». That confirms them both dead by 1848. He is the miller who declared Giuseppe Ventrice's death in 1831 (Briatico Morti 1831, atto 12), so he knew the family already. Nothing is known of any children, and none has been sought. A Rosario Comerci, 50, son of the late Francesco Comerci and the late Catarina Mannella, died at Briatico on 3 February 1845 (Morti 1845, atto 2, read by a delegated reader, not yet checked at the image): probably his brother, not added as a person. Placed at Briatico, where he was born and lived. HIS FIRST WIFE WAS SAVERIA LUCIFARO, who died on 16 December 1817 (Briatico Morti 1817, atto 39, image 21, read at the image): the act names the husband only as «Comerci», but Giacomo Comerci, 36, miller, signs as «marito della difonta», and her father Antonio Lucifaro, 56, a miller, is the other declarant. When Antonio Lucifaro himself died on 29 March 1818 (Morti 1818, atto 10, read by a delegated reader) Giacomo Comerci, 37, miller, declared it as «genero del defunto». By November 1819 he was a «vaticale» of 34 with a wife Caterina Polito and newborn twin sons who both died at five days. TWO MEN OF THE NAME LIVED IN BRIATICO in 1817-18, a «maggiore» of about sixty and a «minore»; the miller is the «minore», and his age fits this man, who died in 1848 at about seventy. The ages of one man swing between thirty-four and thirty-seven in three years, and nothing in the acts proves the 1817 husband of Saveria is the same man as the 1838 bridegroom beyond the name, the trade and the age. HIS SON FRANCESCO, a miller born at Briatico, died on 7 September 1827 (Briatico Morti 1827, atto 21, an_ua87685, image 13, read at the image): «figlio di Giacomo Comerci, mugnajo, e di Saveria Lucifero», which proves the miller of 1817 and this family are one household.

His wife was Caterina Mannella, who died on 16 February 1825. DEAD BY SEPTEMBER 1817, and his death has not been found: it is not in the acts of Briatico Morti 1816 (19 acts, from 3 April) or 1817 (40 acts), which were read for it, so it is before that, in 1809-15 or in the first months of 1816, if Briatico recorded it. His trade is «bracciale» in his son Rosario's death act of 1845.

name: Caterina Mannella
bornNote: SIXTY-FOUR at her death («di anni sessantaquattro»), so born about 1761; the place is not stated.
source: Briatico, Morti 1825, atto 6 (an_ua87683, image 5, LEFT page; read at the image by the session); Briatico, Matrimoni 1838, atto 2 (an_ua87652, image 3); Briatico, Morti 1817 (an_ua87675, image 16)
note: FOUND: DIED 16 FEBRUARY 1825 AT BRIATICO, aged sixty-four, in the house of her son Rosario Comerci. Act 6 of Briatico Morti 1825, read at the image, calls her «figlia di Antonino [Mannella], defonto, e di Anna Polito, defonta»: BOTH HER PARENTS ARE NAMED, which gives this line a generation it did not have. She is the mother of Giacomo Comerci, Rosario Comerci and Arcangelo Comerci (her son Arcangelo's death act of 15 September 1817 names her with no «fu», so she was alive then, and Giacomo's marriage act of 1838 and death act of 1848 call her «defunta»). The act does not name her husband Francesco Comerci. Of the Mannella deaths read in Briatico in 1818 (Antonino, 22, son of Francesco Mannella and the late Concetta Lauda; Giuseppa, 50, daughter of the late Vincenzo Mannella; the child Vincenzo), none is shown to belong to her family and none is claimed.

name: Giovanni Ventrice (died unmarried, 1849)
bornNote: BORN AT BRIATICO at eight o'clock in the morning of 24 June 1826 (Briatico Nati 1826, atto 21, an_ua87728, image 22, read at the image by the session): a boy, declared by a midwife, Rosa Veterale? (about 70, spinner), born to «Caterina Cichello», 26, and «Giuseppe Ventrice», given as «ventidue» (22: a doubtful reading, and unlike the 34 of 1824, the 33 of 1828 and the 32 of 1830), a vetturale («vaticale»), both of Briatico, in their own house; baptised at S. Nicola the same day as «Giovanni Ventrica». Witnesses D. Giuseppe Consoli and D. Domenico Consoli, proprietors. He died at ten o'clock on 10 November 1849 in his own house, «celibe» (unmarried), domiciled at Briatico, five months after his sister's marriage; the act names his father as «Giuseppe Ventrice, bracciale, defunto» and his mother as «Caterina Cichello», domiciled at Briatico, so she was alive.
